distractorReasons: 快諾の応答で、Hold those two cornersという具体的な共同作業に自然につながる。
弁当箱で手がふさがっていると断ったならThanks! Hold those two cornersと矛盾。
これから広げる提案はたたむ場面と逆。
すでにかばんにしまったなら今から角を持ってたたむ状況と矛盾。
items.translation: A：カイト、この大きなレジャーシートをたたむのを手伝ってくれる？B：いいよ、この風の中で一人でたたむのは大変だよね！A：ありがとう！向こうの2つの角を持って私のほうへ歩いてきて。

items.prompt:
A: Have you seen Ms. Mori this morning? I need her signature on our club form.
B: (     )
A: Thanks! I'll check there before first period starts.
choices: I handed my form to Mr. Takahashi yesterday afternoon.
You need to write the club captain's name at the top first.
She was printing handouts in the workroom five minutes ago.
She is taking the third-year students on a trip all week.
items.explanation: 森先生を見かけたか尋ねられ、「5分前に作業室でプリントを刷っていらしたよ」と教え、「1時間目が始まる前にそこを見に行ってみるね」と続く会話。
distractorReasons: 昨日高橋先生に出した話では森先生の居場所にならない。
部長名の記入注意ではcheck thereにつながらない。
check thereのthere（the workroom）を指す具体的な居場所情報になっている。
今週ずっと修学旅行で不在なら1時間目前にそこへ行く返答と矛盾。
items.translation: A：今朝、森先生を見かけた？部活の届出書に先生のサインが必要なんだ。B：5分前に作業室でプリントを印刷していらしたよ。A：ありがとう！1時間目が始まる前にそこへ行ってみるね。

items.prompt:
A: How did your homemade bread turn out yesterday, Yuna?
B: (     )
A: Don't worry. My first loaf was hard too before I learned how much yeast to use.
choices: Everyone in my family said it was soft and fluffy inside.
It smelled great, though the crust came out a bit too hard.
The bakery in front of the station was already sold out.
I ran out of flour, so I baked blueberry muffins instead.

駅前のパン屋が売り切れだった話は自宅の手作りパンの質問と合わない。
代わりにマフィンを焼いたならパンが硬かった励ましと噛み合わない。

items.prompt:
A: Why are we taking the west staircase instead of the center one?
B: (     )

The west staircase is closer to the bicycle parking lot.

items.prompt: How does the town prevent lanterns from flowing out into the sea?
choices: Lanterns are kept inside a gymnasium instead of the river.
Visitors tie long ropes to their lanterns from the bridge.
The lanterns dissolve completely in river water.
Volunteer boats collect all the lanterns downstream at 8:30 p.m.
items.explanation: 海へ流出しないよう、午後8時30分に200メートル下流でボランティアのボートがすべての灯籠を回収する仕組みになっている。
distractorReasons: 体育館で行うのではない。
橋から長いロープを結ぶのではない。
水に溶ける紙ではない（希望者は持ち帰れる）。
all lanterns are collected by volunteer boats two hundred meters downstream at 8:30 p.m.と一致。
items.translation: 灯籠が海へ流れ出ないように、町はどのような対策をとっていますか。

passage.title: Town River Lantern Evening
passage.text:
CLEARWATER TOWN CULTURAL COMMITTEE
Town River Lantern Evening
Date: Saturday, August 8 (6:30 p.m. – 8:30 p.m.)
Place: Stepping-Stone Lawn beside Clearwater Bridge

Come celebrate summer evening by floating paper lanterns illuminated with reusable LED lights! From 5:30 p.m., visitors can decorate a wooden-base paper lantern with brush pens for 300 yen at the riverside tent.

Environmental Promise: Unlike traditional candles, all lanterns are collected by volunteer boats two hundred meters downstream at 8:30 p.m. so nothing flows out to sea. If you would like to keep your decorated paper shade as a souvenir, bring your numbered ticket stub to the tent between 8:35 p.m. and 9:00 p.m.
passage.translation: クリアウォーター町文化委員会 川の灯籠流し夕べ。8月8日（土）午後6時30分〜8時30分、クリアウォーター橋横の芝生広場。再利用可能なLEDライトで灯す紙灯籠を流して夏の宵を祝いましょう。午後5時30分から川辺のテントにて300円で木製台座の紙灯籠に筆ペンで絵や文字を描けます。環境への約束：従来のろうそくと異なり、海にゴミが流出しないよう午後8時30分に200メートル下流でボランティアの舟が全灯籠を回収します。絵を描いた紙カバーを記念に持ち帰りたい方は、午後8時35分〜9時の間に番号付き半券をテントへお持ちください。

items.prompt: What should visitors do if they want to take their decorated paper shade home?
choices: Show their numbered ticket stub at the tent between 8:35 p.m. and 9:00 p.m.
Take it out of the river themselves before 7:00 p.m.
Come back to Clearwater Bridge the next morning.
Pay an extra 1,000 yen before decorating it.
items.explanation: 絵を描いた紙シェードを記念に持ち帰りたい場合は、午後8時35分〜9時00分の間に番号付き半券をテントへ持参する。
distractorReasons: bring your numbered ticket stub to the tent between 8:35 p.m. and 9:00 p.m.と一致。
自分で川に入って拾うのではない。
翌朝取りに来るのではない。
1,000円の追加料金はない。
items.translation: 絵を描いた紙カバーを家に持ち帰りたい場合、来場者はどうすればよいですか。

passage.title: Preparing the Graduation Photo Slideshow
passage.text:
From: Kaito
To: Riko
Subject: Music and photos for the Grade 9 farewell assembly

Hi Riko,
Thanks for collecting the sports day and school trip photos from all four ninth-grade classes! I put the eighty photos into our slideshow software last night, and the whole video is about six minutes long.

When I showed a test version to Mr. Honda at lunch today, he really liked the order of the scenes, but he noticed two small things we should fix before Friday's rehearsal. First, three photos from Class 9C's chorus contest are a little dark, so I will brighten them tonight on my computer. Second, we still need one cheerful instrumental song to play during the club-activity section in the middle.

Since your older brother plays trumpet in the brass band club, do you think we could use the recording of their autumn concert march? Please ask him tonight if the band adviser allows us to use two minutes of that recording!

Talk to you tomorrow,
Kaito
passage.translation: 差出人カイト、宛先リコ、件名：3年生を送る会の写真スライドショーについて。3年生全4クラスから体育祭や修学旅行の写真を集めてくれてありがとう！昨夜80枚の写真をスライド作成ソフトに入れ、全体で約6分の映像になった。今日の昼に本田先生へ試作版を見せたところ構成はとても褒めてもらえたが、金曜のリハーサル前に直すべき点が2つ見つかった。1つ目は3年C組の合唱コンクールの写真3枚が少し暗いため、今夜僕のパソコンで明るく補正する。2つ目は中盤の部活動紹介パートで流す明るい器楽曲がまだ1曲必要なこと。リコのお兄さんは吹奏楽部でトランペットを吹いているから、秋の定期演奏会のマーチの録音を使わせてもらえないかな。その録音を2分間使ってよいか吹奏楽部の顧問の先生が許可してくださるか、今夜お兄さんに聞いてみてほしい！

passage.title: Table Tennis in the Old School Gym
passage.text:
Five years ago, North Valley Elementary School closed because fewer children lived in the mountain village, and students began riding a school bus to a larger town nearby. Although the classrooms were turned into a small local library, the wooden gymnasium behind the building stayed locked and silent.

Last autumn, fourteen-year-old Soma found four dusty table-tennis tables folded up in the gym's storage room while helping his aunt return library books. Soma loved playing table tennis at his junior high school, yet he had nowhere to practice on weekends without taking a forty-minute bus ride.

Soma wrote a polite proposal to the village council suggesting a "Saturday Morning Open Gym." Retired carpenter Mr. Endo offered to check the floorboards and replace the torn nets, while Soma and two friends made simple posters inviting anyone from age seven to eighty. Only six people showed up on the first Saturday in November, but word spread quickly.

items.prompt: What gave Soma the idea to open the gym on Saturday mornings?

His bus driver asked him to clean the library windows.
Mr. Endo gave him a brand-new paddle for his birthday.
His teacher assigned a report about Olympic table-tennis players.
items.explanation: おばの本返却を手伝った際、体育館の用具室に4台の卓球台が折りたたんで保管されているのを見つけたのがきっかけ。
distractorReasons: found four dusty table-tennis tables folded up in the gym's storage roomと一致。
運転手の依頼ではない。
誕生日プレゼントではない。
オリンピック選手の宿題ではない。
items.translation: ソウマが土曜日の午前中に体育館を開放しようと思いついたきっかけは何ですか。

items.prompt: How did Mr. Endo help prepare for the Saturday sessions?
choices: He drove forty villagers to town in his school bus.
He bought four new tables from a sports store.
He checked the wooden floor and put up new nets on the tables.
He wrote posters in three languages for tourists.
items.explanation: 引退した大工の遠藤さんが体育館の床板を点検し、破れていた卓球ネットを新しいものに交換してくれた。
distractorReasons: バス運転ではない。
新しい卓球台4台の購入ではない。
check the floorboards and replace the torn netsと一致。
観光客向け3か国語ポスターではない。
items.translation: 遠藤さんは土曜日の開放に向けた準備をどのように手伝いましたか。

items.prompt: What surprised the teenagers once twenty villagers started coming each week?
choices: Elementary school children could lift the heavy tables alone.
Older residents could hit clever spin serves from their younger days.
The library decided to throw away all its books.
Nobody in the village had ever seen a table-tennis ball before.
items.explanation: 20代のころに卓球をしていた高齢住民たちが、中学生も驚くような変化球サーブ（tricky spin serves）を打てたこと。
distractorReasons: 小学生が一人で重い台を持ち上げた話はない。
turned out to have tricky spin serves that surprised the teenagersと一致。
図書室の本廃棄の話はない。
誰も球を見たことがなかったのではない。
items.translation: 毎週20人の村民が集まるようになると、中学生たちは何に驚きましたか。

items.prompt: What is the main point of this story?
choices: Teenagers can improve at sports only if they practice alone.
Mountain villages should build larger bus terminals instead of libraries.
Wooden gymnasiums are too cold to use during winter.
A student's idea turned an unused building into a lively place for all ages.
items.explanation: 中学生の提案をきっかけに、眠っていた閉校体育館が子どもから高齢者まで世代を超えて楽しく交流する場としてよみがえったという物語。
distractorReasons: 一人で練習すべきという話とは逆。
バスターミナル建設の話ではない。
雪の冬の朝にも賑わっている。
未使用だった体育館が多世代の温かい交流拠点になった本文全体の趣旨と一致。
items.translation: この物語が伝えている中心的な内容は何ですか。

items.prompt: 外国人の友達（Yuna）から以下のEメールを受け取りました。Eメールを読み、それに対する返信メールを英文で書きなさい。返信メールの中で、友達（Yuna）からの2つの質問（下線部）に対応する内容を、あなた自身で自由に考えて答えなさい。（目安語数：15〜25語）

passage.title: E-mail from Yuna
passage.text:
Hi,
Thank you for your e-mail.
You said that you went to a school orchestra concert yesterday! __Which musical instrument sounded the best to you?__ __And where did you sit in the hall?__
Your friend,
Yuna
passage.translation: こんにちは。Eメールをありがとう。昨日、学校のオーケストラ演奏会に行ったと言っていましたね！あなたにはどの楽器の音が一番素敵に聞こえましたか。また、ホールのどのあたりに座りましたか。あなたの友人、ユナより

items.model: The cello sounded the best to me because its tone was warm. I sat near the middle of the first floor.
items.translation: 音色が温かかったので、私にはチェロの音が一番素敵に聞こえました。1階の真ん中あたりの席に座りました。
items.explanation: 1つ目の質問（一番よく聞こえた楽器：チェロ）と2つ目の質問（座った場所：1階中央付近）に過去形で正確に答えています（21語）。
rubric: 1つ目の質問（一番素敵に聞こえた楽器）に答えた
2つ目の質問（ホールで座った場所）に答えた
sounded / satなど過去時制と前置詞句が正確である
15〜25語の目安に収まっている

items.prompt:
次のQUESTIONについて、あなたの考えとその理由を2つ英文で書きなさい。（目安語数：25〜35語）
QUESTION: What school event do you enjoy the most?
items.model: I enjoy our school chorus contest the most. First, practicing songs every day brings my classmates closer together. Second, singing on a big stage feels exciting.
items.translation: 私は学校の合唱コンクールを一番楽しんでいます。第一に、毎日歌を練習することでクラスメート同士の仲が深まります。第二に、大きなステージで歌うのはワクワクするからです。
items.explanation: 一番楽しい学校行事として合唱コンクールを挙げ、First（毎日の練習でクラスの絆が深まる）とSecond（大きなステージで歌う高揚感）の2つの理由を26語で述べています。
rubric: 一番楽しむ学校行事を明確に書いた
1つ目の理由を具体的に書いた
2つ目の理由を具体的に書いた
25〜35語の目安に収まっている

items.prompt: The train was delayed, but we (     ) reached the hotel before midnight.
items.explanation: 遅延したものの最終的に到着したのでeventually。
distractorReasons: eventuallyは最終的に。遅延後の結果を表す。
recentlyは最近。遅延から到着への展開でない。
immediatelyは直ちに。遅れた状況と合わない。
regularlyは定期的に。1回の到着でない。
items.translation: 列車は遅れましたが、最終的に深夜前にホテルへ着きました。

items.prompt: The company offers free training to help new employees (     ) their skills.
items.explanation: 研修で技能を向上させるのでdevelop。
distractorReasons: divideは分割する。技能向上の意味でない。
develop skillsで技能を伸ばす。
deliverは配達する。
describeは説明する。研修の目的は向上。
items.translation: 会社は新入社員の技能向上のため無料研修を提供しています。

items.prompt: The museum does not allow visitors (     ) photographs in this room.
items.explanation: allow＋人＋to不定詞。
distractorReasons: allow visitors takingとはしない。
原形の前にtoが必要。
allow visitors to takeで撮影を許可する。
takenは過去分詞で接続できない。
items.translation: 博物館はこの部屋での来訪者の写真撮影を許可していません。

items.prompt: The manager asked us to (     ) a solution before the next meeting.
items.explanation: 解決策を考え出すのでcome up with。
distractorReasons: look down onは見下す。
run out ofは使い果たす。
get away withは罰を受けずに済む。
come up with a solutionで解決策を考え出す。
items.translation: 管理者は次の会議までに解決策を考え出すよう私たちに求めました。

items.prompt: I would rather walk to the station (     ) wait another hour for the bus.
items.explanation: would rather A than BでBよりAしたい。
distractorReasons: thanが比較する行動をつなぐ。
asではratherとの対応がない。
fromは行動の比較をつなげない。
whileはこの構文で比較を作らない。
items.translation: バスをもう1時間待つくらいなら駅まで歩きたいです。

items.prompt: The doctor gave me some (     ) on how to improve my sleep.
items.explanation: someの後、睡眠改善に関する助言という名詞advice。
distractorReasons: adviseは動詞。
adviceは不可算名詞の助言。
advancingは進むこと。医師からの助言に合わない。
advisedは動詞の過去形・過去分詞。
items.translation: 医師は睡眠を改善する方法について助言をくれました。

items.prompt: This machine is quite (     ). It has worked without a problem for ten years.
items.explanation: 10年間問題なく動くので信頼できるreliable。
distractorReasons: temporaryは一時的。長期使用の説明と逆。
emptyは空の。動作実績から導けない。
reliableは信頼性が高い。
narrowは幅が狭い。故障しないことの説明でない。
items.translation: この機械はとても信頼できます。10年間問題なく動いています。

items.prompt: By the time I arrived at the classroom, the lesson (     ).
items.explanation: 過去の到着より前に開始済みなので過去完了。
distractorReasons: 現在形では過去の前後関係を示せない。
未来形では到着時に開始済みにならない。
現在完了の基準時は現在。
had startedは過去より前の開始。
items.translation: 教室に着くまでに授業はもう始まっていました。

items.prompt: The town is trying to (     ) the number of cars in the city center.
items.explanation: 中心部の車の数を減らす政策なのでreduce。
distractorReasons: reduce the numberで数を減らす。
inventは発明する。
attendは出席する。
contain the numberとはこの意味で使わない。
items.translation: 町は中心部の車の数を減らそうとしています。

items.prompt: Please let me know (     ) you will be able to attend the workshop or not.
items.explanation: whether ... or notで〜かどうか。
distractorReasons: whatは何を。出席可否を表さない。
whetherがor notと対応する。
whichは選択対象を必要とする。
whoseは誰の。所有を尋ねていない。
items.translation: 講習会に出席できるかどうか知らせてください。

items.prompt: The hotel was fully booked, so we had no (     ) but to stay somewhere else.
items.explanation: have no choice but toで〜せざるを得ない。
distractorReasons: methodではこの定型表現にならない。
reasonなら理由がないで意味が逆。
no choice but toは選択の余地がない。
requestは依頼で定型に合わない。
items.translation: ホテルは満室だったので、ほかに泊まるしかありませんでした。

items.prompt: This backpack is expensive, but it is worth (     ) because it will last a long time.
items.explanation: be worth＋動名詞で〜する価値がある。
distractorReasons: 原形はworthに直接続けない。
worthの後はto不定詞でない。
過去分詞では購入という行為を表せない。

passage.title: A Different Kind of Team
passage.text:
When Hana joined her school's outdoor club, she expected to spend every weekend hiking in the mountains. At the first meeting, however, the leader announced that the club would help make a walking trail near the town library. Hana was disappointed. She thought working close to home would be less exciting than visiting distant places.

On the first workday, the members met Mr. Lee, who used a wheelchair. He explained that the old trail was too narrow and uneven for him to use. The club's task was not simply to make the path look nicer. It was to (21). Hana had never considered that a small change to a path could make such a difference.

The work took several weeks. The members measured the path, removed stones, and built a resting area. At the opening event, Mr. Lee traveled along the new trail with his family. Watching them, Hana realized that the project had been (22). She still enjoyed mountain trips, but she now understood why the leader had chosen this local activity.

passage.title: Changes to the Food Festival
passage.text:
From: Luis, Festival Coordinator
To: Volunteers
Subject: Please read before Saturday

Dear volunteers,
Thank you for helping at our international food festival. There have been two important changes. First, heavy rain is expected, so the festival will take place inside the community center rather than in the park. The center has enough space for all the food tables, but the entrance is narrow. Please arrive at the back door to help move supplies.

Second, the local bus company cannot provide the extra morning service we requested. Some visitors may arrive later than planned. We will therefore begin serving food at 11:30 instead of 11:00. Volunteers should still arrive at 9:00, as originally arranged. We need that time to set up the tables and check the kitchen equipment.

If you are helping at a food table, please bring a clean apron. We will provide gloves and name tags. Volunteers at the information desk do not need aprons. Those who have not yet chosen a job should contact me by Thursday evening.

Finally, please avoid bringing your own cars because parking spaces must be kept for delivery vehicles. The number 6 bus stops directly outside the center. I will send a map with the entrance marked tomorrow.

Best wishes,
Luis
passage.translation: ボランティア各位。国際フードフェスティバルへの協力への感謝と二つの変更。大雨予報のため公園でなく公民館内で実施。テーブルの場所は十分だが入口が狭いので、裏口から物資搬入を手伝ってほしい。朝のバス増便がなく一部の客が遅れるため、料理の提供を11時から11時30分へ変更。ただしスタッフ集合は当初どおり9時で、設営と厨房機器の確認に時間が必要。料理担当は清潔なエプロンを持参し、手袋と名札は支給。案内担当はエプロン不要。担当未定の人は木曜夜までに連絡。配送車用の駐車場所を確保するため自家用車は避ける。6番バスが正面に停車。入口を示す地図を翌日送付する。

items.translation: 職員が最初に気づいた問題は何ですか。

passage.title: A Museum You Can Hear
passage.text:
At the Riverside Museum, most visitors once followed signs from one glass case to another. They read short descriptions of old tools, clothes, and furniture, then moved on. The objects were interesting, but the museum staff noticed that many visitors did not stay long. Few people understood how the objects had been used in daily life.

To change this, the museum invited local residents to record stories about familiar objects. One woman described the sound of the sewing machine her mother used at home. A retired baker explained why a wooden tray had a particular shape. These recordings were added to a small audio player that visitors could borrow at the entrance. The aim was not to replace the written descriptions but to provide another way to explore the collection.

The first recordings were long and difficult to follow. Staff had assumed that visitors would listen to complete interviews. In practice, people wanted to move at their own speed. The museum therefore divided the interviews into short sections. Each section focused on one object and lasted less than two minutes. Visitors could choose only the stories that interested them.

The new system also changed the relationship between the museum and the town. Residents who had rarely visited came to hear their relatives' recordings. Some brought photographs or offered to share their own memories. The museum checked these stories against old records before using them, because personal memories are not always exact.

A visitor survey later showed that people were spending more time in the museum. However, the director did not regard longer visits as the only sign of success. She was more pleased that visitors were asking new questions about everyday life in the past. The museum now plans to add stories from younger residents as well. The staff believe that objects which seem ordinary today may help future visitors understand the present.
passage.translation: リバーサイド博物館の来館者は、展示ケースを巡って道具や衣服、家具の短い説明を読むだけで、滞在は短く、昔の生活での使われ方を理解する人は少数でした。改善のため住民の体験談を録音。母のミシンの音やパン屋の木製トレーの形の理由などを入口で貸すプレーヤーに収録しました。文章を置き換えるのでなく別の見方を加える目的です。最初は録音が長く、来館者が自分の速度で移動したいと分かったため、物一つにつき2分未満の短い録音に分割し、興味のある話を選べるようにしました。親族の録音を聞きに来る住民が増え、写真や思い出の提供にもつながりました。ただし個人の記憶は正確とは限らず、古い記録と照合しています。調査では滞在時間が伸びましたが、館長はそれだけでなく昔の日常生活への新しい質問が出ることを喜びました。今は若い住民の話も追加する予定です。今日の普通の物が将来の来館者に今を理解させると考えています。

A visitor survey later showed that people were spending more time in the museum. However, the director did not regard longer visits as the only sign of success. She was more pleased that visitors were asking new questions about everyday life in the past. The museum now plans to add stories from younger residents as well. The staff believe that objects which seem ordinary today may help future visitors understand the present.
passage.translation: リバーサイド博物館の来館者は、展示ケースを巡って道具や衣服、家具の短い説明を読むだけで、滞在は短く、昔の生活での使われ方を理解する人は少数でした。改善のため住民の体験談を録音。母のミシンの音やパン屋の木製トレーの形の理由などを入口で貸すプレーヤーに収録しました。文章を置き換えるのでなく別の見方を加える目的です。最初は録音が長く、来館者が自分の速度で移動したいと分かったため、物一つにつき2分未満の短い録音に分割し、興味のある話を選べるようにしました。親族の録音を聞きに来る住民が増え、写真や思い出の提供にもつながりました。ただし個人の記憶は正確とは限らず、古い記録と照合しています。調査では滞在時間が伸びましたが、館長はそれだけでなく昔の日常生活への新しい質問が出ることを喜びました。今は若い住民の話も追加する予定です。今日の普通の物が将来の来館者に今を理解させると考えています。

passage.title: A Museum You Can Hear
passage.text:
At the Riverside Museum, most visitors once followed signs from one glass case to another. They read short descriptions of old tools, clothes, and furniture, then moved on. The objects were interesting, but the museum staff noticed that many visitors did not stay long. Few people understood how the objects had been used in daily life.

To change this, the museum invited local residents to record stories about familiar objects. One woman described the sound of the sewing machine her mother used at home. A retired baker explained why a wooden tray had a particular shape. These recordings were added to a small audio player that visitors could borrow at the entrance. The aim was not to replace the written descriptions but to provide another way to explore the collection.

The first recordings were long and difficult to follow. Staff had assumed that visitors would listen to complete interviews. In practice, people wanted to move at their own speed. The museum therefore divided the interviews into short sections. Each section focused on one object and lasted less than two minutes. Visitors could choose only the stories that interested them.

The new system also changed the relationship between the museum and the town. Residents who had rarely visited came to hear their relatives' recordings. Some brought photographs or offered to share their own memories. The museum checked these stories against old records before using them, because personal memories are not always exact.

A visitor survey later showed that people were spending more time in the museum. However, the director did not regard longer visits as the only sign of success. She was more pleased that visitors were asking new questions about everyday life in the past. The museum now plans to add stories from younger residents as well. The staff believe that objects which seem ordinary today may help future visitors understand the present.

items.prompt:
次のQUESTIONについて、あなたの意見とその理由を2つ英文で書きなさい。（目安語数：50〜60語）
QUESTION: Do you think it is a good idea for high school students to study at a cafe?
items.model: I think it is a good idea for high school students to study at a cafe. First, a quiet change of environment helps them concentrate better than staying in their bedrooms all day. Second, there are fewer distractions such as television or video games at home, so they can finish their homework efficiently.
items.translation: 私は高校生がカフェで勉強するのはよい考えだと思います。第一に、静かに環境を変えることで、一日中自分の部屋にいるよりも集中しやすくなります。第二に、家にあるテレビやテレビゲームのような気を散らすものが少ないため、効率よく宿題を終えられます。
items.explanation: 冒頭で賛成の立場を明示し、First（環境変化による集中力の維持）とSecond（家庭内の誘惑からの切り離しによる効率化）の2つの異なる理由を因果関係とともに展開しています。
rubric: QUESTIONに対する賛成・反対の立場を冒頭で明示した
異なる2つの理由をFirst / Second等で整理して述べた

passage.title: A Second Life for Sports Gear
passage.text:
Many children try a new sport at school, only to outgrow their shoes, rackets, or protective pads within a single year. Because brand-new equipment can be costly, some families hesitate to let children try unfamiliar sports. Noticeably usable gear often ends up sitting in closets long after young players have moved on.

In the town of Brookside, two high school coaches started a seasonal "Gear Swap Day" at the public gym. Families donate clean sports items they no longer need, and any child in town can select suitable equipment at no charge. Before anything is placed on the tables, volunteer coaches inspect helmets, straps, and soles carefully. Their priority is to (21). Items that are worn out or damaged are recycled rather than passed on.

Over the past two years, participation in beginner sports classes in Brookside has risen steadily. Parents say children feel freer to experiment when trying a sport does not require an expensive initial purchase. For the coaches, the swap has proved (22), helping young residents stay active regardless of household budgets.

passage.title: A Second Life for Sports Gear
passage.text:
Many children try a new sport at school, only to outgrow their shoes, rackets, or protective pads within a single year. Because brand-new equipment can be costly, some families hesitate to let children try unfamiliar sports. Noticeably usable gear often ends up sitting in closets long after young players have moved on.

In the town of Brookside, two high school coaches started a seasonal "Gear Swap Day" at the public gym. Families donate clean sports items they no longer need, and any child in town can select suitable equipment at no charge. Before anything is placed on the tables, volunteer coaches inspect helmets, straps, and soles carefully. Their priority is to (21). Items that are worn out or damaged are recycled rather than passed on.

Over the past two years, participation in beginner sports classes in Brookside has risen steadily. Parents say children feel freer to experiment when trying a sport does not require an expensive initial purchase. For the coaches, the swap has proved (22), helping young residents stay active regardless of household budgets.

passage.title: Notice About the Summer Library Internship
passage.text:
From: Hannah Cole, Youth Services Librarian
To: High School Interns
Subject: Orientation and schedule update

Dear interns,
Welcome to the Harbor Library summer internship program! Before your shifts begin next week, all interns must attend a ninety-minute orientation this Friday from 2:00 p.m. to 3:30 p.m. in Meeting Room C. During the session, we will practice using the checkout scanner and review how to assist elementary school children choosing summer reading books.

Please note one change to the schedule sent last month. Because the air-conditioning unit on the third floor will undergo repairs on Monday and Tuesday, the quiet study hall there will be closed on those two days. Interns originally assigned to the third floor on Monday or Tuesday will help organize the picture-book corner on the first floor instead.

Each intern will receive an official library badge on Friday. Please wear a collared shirt and comfortable shoes; sandals are not permitted for safety reasons when moving book carts. You may store lunches in the staff break room refrigerator, provided your container is clearly labeled with your name.

If an unexpected school commitment prevents you from attending Friday's orientation, please reply by Wednesday noon so we can arrange a brief make-up briefing on Thursday afternoon.

Warm regards,
Hannah Cole
passage.translation: 差出人ハンナ・コール（青少年担当司書）、宛先高校生インターン各位、件名：オリエンテーションと予定変更のお知らせ。来週のシフト開始前に、全員今週金曜午後2時〜3時30分に会議室Cの90分間のオリエンテーションへ出席すること。貸出スキャナーの操作練習と、夏休みの本を選ぶ小学生への案内方法を確認する。先月送付した予定から1点変更あり：月曜・火曜に3階の空調設備の修理が行われるため3階自習室は2日間閉鎖となり、その日の3階担当者は代わりに1階の絵本コーナー整理を手伝う。金曜に公式バッジを配布する。襟付きシャツと歩きやすい靴を着用すること（ブックカート運搬時の安全上サンダル不可）。昼食は名前を明記した容器であれば職員休憩室の冷蔵庫に保管可能。急な学校用事で金曜に出席できない場合は、木曜午後に短い代替説明を組めるよう水曜正午までに返信すること。

passage.title: Why Small Bakeries Are Changing Their Schedules
passage.text:
In many towns, traditional bakeries used to display full trays of every kind of bread from early morning until closing time. Customers appreciated seeing abundant choices even late in the afternoon. Behind the scenes, however, keeping shelves full all day meant that unsold loaves frequently had to be thrown away at night, increasing ingredient costs and food waste.

Recently, a growing number of independent bakers have moved away from this model. At Sunrise Crust Bakery, for example, the owner noticed from sales records that crusty dinner rolls sold mostly after four o'clock, whereas fruit pastries were popular before ten in the morning. Instead of baking everything at dawn and hoping it would sell, the bakery began baking smaller batches tailored to each time of day.

At first, the owner worried that customers would complain if a particular item ran out early. When the bakery placed a simple chalkboard schedule outside the door showing what came out of the oven at 8:00 a.m., noon, and 4:00 p.m., customers reacted positively. Commuters started timing their visits to buy warm bread straight from the oven.

To handle the small amount of bread still left at closing time, Sunrise Crust partnered with a nearby evening soup kitchen and offered next-morning "surprise bags" at half price. While small-batch baking requires more careful planning by kitchen staff, the owner found that cutting daily waste allowed the shop to buy higher-quality local flour without raising prices.

Food researchers note that customers' expectations play a major role in reducing retail waste. When shoppers understand that an empty tray late in the day reflects careful production rather than poor service, neighborhood shops can operate far more sustainably.
passage.translation: 多くの町で従来のパン屋は早朝から閉店まで全種類のパンをトレーいっぱいに並べていた。客は夕方遅くでも豊富な選択肢を喜んだが、裏側では売れ残りのパンを毎晩廃棄せざるを得ず、材料費と食品ロスを押し上げていた。近年、独立系ベーカリーの多くがこの方式を見直している。たとえばサンライズ・クラスト・ベーカリーでは、売上データから食事用ロールパンは主に午後4時以降に売れ、フルーツデニッシュは午前10時前に人気だと分かった。夜明けに全種類を大量に焼くのではなく、時間帯ごとの需要に合わせた少量焼き立て方式に切り替えた。当初店主は早めの品切れへの苦情を懸念したが、午前8時・正午・午後4時の焼き上がり予定表を店先の黒板に掲示すると好評で、通勤客も焼き立てを狙って来店するようになった。閉店時にわずかに残るパンは近隣の夜間食堂への提供や翌朝半額の「お楽しみ袋」で活用した。少量多頻度焼成には職人の綿密な計画が要るものの、廃棄削減で浮いた費用により値上げせず高品質な地元産小麦粉を仕入れられるようになった。研究者は、夕方の空のトレーを「サービス不足」ではなく「計画的な生産の証し」と買い物客が理解することが小売店の持続可能性を支えると指摘する。

It required all customers to order bread a week ahead.
items.explanation: 夜明けにまとめて焼く代わりに、時間帯ごとの売れ行きに合わせて少量ずつ焼く方式に変えた。
distractorReasons: baking smaller batches tailored to each time of dayと一致。
週2日営業への短縮はない。
フルーツペストリーは午前中の人気商品として継続している。
1週間前の事前注文制にはしていない。
items.translation: サンライズ・クラスト・ベーカリーはパンの焼き方をどのように変えましたか。

passage.translation: 多くの町で従来のパン屋は早朝から閉店まで全種類のパンをトレーいっぱいに並べていた。客は夕方遅くでも豊富な選択肢を喜んだが、裏側では売れ残りのパンを毎晩廃棄せざるを得ず、材料費と食品ロスを押し上げていた。近年、独立系ベーカリーの多くがこの方式を見直している。たとえばサンライズ・クラスト・ベーカリーでは、売上データから食事用ロールパンは主に午後4時以降に売れ、フルーツデニッシュは午前10時前に人気だと分かった。夜明けに全種類を大量に焼くのではなく、時間帯ごとの需要に合わせた少量焼き立て方式に切り替えた。当初店主は早めの品切れへの苦情を懸念したが、午前8時・正午・午後4時の焼き上がり予定表を店先の黒板に掲示すると好評で、通勤客も焼き立てを狙って来店するようになった。閉店時にわずかに残るパンは近隣の夜間食堂への提供や翌朝半額の「お楽しみ袋」で活用した。少量多頻度焼成には職人の綿密な計画が要るものの、廃棄削減で浮いた費用により値上げせず高品質な地元産小麦粉を仕入れられるようになった。研究者は、夕方の空のトレーを「サービス不足」ではなく「計画的な生産の証し」と買い物客が理解することが小売店の持続可能性を支えると指摘する。

items.prompt: What benefit did reducing daily waste bring to Sunrise Crust Bakery?
choices: It could use better local flour without increasing its prices.
It never had a single loaf left at closing time.
It was able to open five new branches overseas.
Kitchen staff no longer needed to plan their work.
items.explanation: 日々の廃棄を減らしたことで、商品の値上げをせずにより高品質な地元産小麦粉を購入できるようになった。
distractorReasons: buy higher-quality local flour without raising pricesと一致。
閉店時に少量残るパン（small amount ... still left）は夜間食堂やお楽しみ袋で活用している。
海外出店の記述はない。
むしろ綿密な計画（more careful planning）が必要と述べられている。
items.translation: 日々の廃棄を減らしたことは、サンライズ・クラスト・ベーカリーにどんな利点をもたらしましたか。

passage.title: Why Small Bakeries Are Changing Their Schedules
passage.text:
In many towns, traditional bakeries used to display full trays of every kind of bread from early morning until closing time. Customers appreciated seeing abundant choices even late in the afternoon. Behind the scenes, however, keeping shelves full all day meant that unsold loaves frequently had to be thrown away at night, increasing ingredient costs and food waste.

Recently, a growing number of independent bakers have moved away from this model. At Sunrise Crust Bakery, for example, the owner noticed from sales records that crusty dinner rolls sold mostly after four o'clock, whereas fruit pastries were popular before ten in the morning. Instead of baking everything at dawn and hoping it would sell, the bakery began baking smaller batches tailored to each time of day.

At first, the owner worried that customers would complain if a particular item ran out early. When the bakery placed a simple chalkboard schedule outside the door showing what came out of the oven at 8:00 a.m., noon, and 4:00 p.m., customers reacted positively. Commuters started timing their visits to buy warm bread straight from the oven.

To handle the small amount of bread still left at closing time, Sunrise Crust partnered with a nearby evening soup kitchen and offered next-morning "surprise bags" at half price. While small-batch baking requires more careful planning by kitchen staff, the owner found that cutting daily waste allowed the shop to buy higher-quality local flour without raising prices.

Food researchers note that customers' expectations play a major role in reducing retail waste. When shoppers understand that an empty tray late in the day reflects careful production rather than poor service, neighborhood shops can operate far more sustainably.

items.prompt: 海外の友人Ryanから届いたEメールを読み、Ryanからの質問に答えるとともに、下線部についてあなたが知りたいことを2つ質問する返信メールを英語で書きなさい。（目安語数：40〜50語）

passage.title: E-mail from Ryan
passage.text:
Hi!
Last weekend, I took part in __a town cycling event__ along the coast with my older brother. The sea breeze felt great! Where do you like riding a bicycle, and how often do you ride one?
Best,
Ryan
passage.translation: こんにちは！先週末、兄と一緒に海岸沿いの町のサイクリングイベントに参加しました。海風がとても心地よかったです！あなたはどこで自転車に乗るのが好きですか。また、どのくらいの頻度で乗りますか。ライアンより

items.model: Hi Ryan, I enjoy riding my bicycle along the river near my house, and I ride it almost every weekend. Your cycling event sounds exciting! How many kilometers did you ride along the coast? Also, were there many young participants in the event?
items.translation: こんにちは、ライアン。私は家の近くの川沿いで自転車に乗るのが好きで、ほぼ毎週末乗っています。サイクリングイベントは楽しそうですね！海岸沿いを何キロ走りましたか。また、若い参加者はたくさんいましたか。
items.explanation: Ryanからの2つの質問（よく乗る場所：家の近くの川沿い／頻度：ほぼ毎週末）に答えた上で、下線部のサイクリングイベントについて走行距離と若い参加者の様子を2つの疑問文で尋ねています（43語）。
rubric: 相手の質問（好きな場所・乗る頻度）に漏れなく答えた
下線部（町のサイクリングイベント）に関する質問を2つ書いた
時制（現在習慣と過去イベントの区別）と疑問文語順が正確である
40〜50語の目安に収まっている

items.prompt:
次のQUESTIONについて、あなたの意見とその理由を2つ英文で書きなさい。（目安語数：50〜60語）
QUESTION: Do you think schools should teach high school students how to manage money?
items.model: I think schools should teach high school students how to manage money wisely. First, many teenagers earn money from part-time jobs, so learning how to save and budget prevents careless spending. Second, understanding bank accounts and credit cards prepares young people to live independently after they graduate from high school.
items.translation: 私は学校が高校生に賢いお金の管理方法を教えるべきだと思います。第一に、多くの十代がアルバイトでお金を稼ぐため、貯蓄や予算立てを学ぶことで無駄遣いを防げます。第二に、銀行口座やクレジットカードの仕組みを理解することは、若者が高校卒業後に自立して暮らす準備になります。
items.explanation: 金銭教育への賛成を冒頭で示し、First（アルバイト収入の貯蓄・予算管理による浪費防止）とSecond（銀行口座やカードの理解による卒業後の自立準備）の2つの理由を51語で論理的に述べています。
rubric: QUESTIONに対する賛否の意見を明確に示した
在学中の実感と卒業後の備えなど異なる理由を2つ挙げた
動名詞主語や不定詞を用いて論理的に説明した
50〜60語の目安に収まっている

items.prompt: Because the ferry schedule varies according to the season, travelers should check the latest timetable in (     ).

items.prompt: The city museum offers audio guides in six languages at no (     ) charge for high school students.

distractorReasons: at no additional chargeで「追加料金なしで」。
awkwardは「気まずい、ぎこちない」。

artificialは「人工的な」。
items.translation: 市立博物館では高校生に対し追加料金なしで6か国語の音声ガイドを提供しています。

items.prompt: My older sister had her wristwatch (     ) at a small shop near the station yesterday.
items.explanation: have＋目的語（her wristwatch）＋過去分詞（repaired）で「〜を修理してもらう」（使役・受動）。時計は修理される側。
distractorReasons: had her wristwatch repairedで「腕時計を修理してもらった」。
原形repairだと目的語が能動的に修理する意味になり不適。
repairingは進行・能動になり不適。
have O to doの形はとらない。

items.explanation: 冷たい風にもかかわらず大勢のボランティアが日曜朝早くに「姿を見せた（集まった）」なのでshow up。
distractorReasons: show intoは「〜の中へ案内する」で目的語が必要。

items.prompt: The hotel clerk politely apologized to the guests for not (     ) able to prepare their rooms before two o'clock.
items.explanation: 前置詞forの後ろに動名詞の否定形not being（for not being able to ...「〜できなかったことに対して」）を置く。
distractorReasons: 前置詞forの直後に原形beは置けない。
過去分詞beenだけでは置けない。
forの後ろにto不定詞は置けない。

items.translation: ホテルのフロント係は午後2時前にお部屋を用意できなかったことを宿泊客に丁寧に詫びました。

items.prompt: From the top of the lighthouse, you can see fishing boats (     ) clearly on sunny mornings.
items.explanation: 副詞clearlyを自然に強める副詞quite（quite clearly「かなりはっきりと」）を選ぶ。
distractorReasons: farは比較級やtooを強めるが原級clearlyは修飾しない。
muchも原級clearlyを直接修飾しない。
quite clearlyで「とてもはっきりと」。
hardは「一生懸命に」。

過去形knewは現在の反事実に使う。

whenever possibleで「できる限りいつでも」。

items.prompt: Regular stretching helps prevent muscles from becoming (     ) during cold winter months.

fluentは「流暢な」。

items.prompt:

A: Thank you so much!

items.translation: A：すみません。バスを降りたとき、12Bの座席の下に灰色の折りたたみ傘を忘れたと思うのですが。B：少々お待ちください。バスがターミナルを出る前に運転手へ無線で連絡してみます。A：本当にありがとうございます！

items.prompt:

A: Congratulations! That shop suits you perfectly.
choices: It was moved to next Friday.
items.explanation: 書店のアルバイト面接がどうだったか聞かれ、「予想以上にうまくいったよ！来週火曜から研修に入れるか店長に聞かれたんだ」と答え祝福される会話。
distractorReasons: 好結果の報告で、直後の研修開始打診とCongratulations!に完全に一致する。
電車に乗り遅れたなら来週火曜から研修開始という展開と矛盾。
誰も採用していないなら研修の打診と矛盾。
来週金曜に延期されたなら今日の面接結果の報告にならない。
items.translation: A：今日の午後の書店アルバイトの面接はどうだった？B：予想以上によかったよ！来週の火曜日から研修を始められるか店長さんに聞かれたんだ。A：おめでとう！あのお店はあなたにぴったりだね。

items.prompt:

mindの質問に対する許可の定型応答Not at all. Go right ahead.で後半とも一致する。
少し肌寒いと断る表現も後半の賛成理由と矛盾。

items.prompt:
A: Why did the tennis club move tomorrow's practice match from 1:00 p.m. to 9:00 a.m.?
B: (     )
A: Smart move. Playing under the midday sun in August is exhausting.

items.prompt:

passage.title: Keeping Migrating Birds Safe Around Glass Buildings
passage.text:
Modern office buildings and school libraries often feature wide glass windows that fill indoor rooms with natural daylight. While bright interiors save electricity and create pleasant spaces for people, large sheets of clear glass pose an unexpected danger to wild birds. Because glass reflects nearby trees and clouds like a mirror, migrating birds frequently mistake windows for open sky and fly into them.

For many years, building managers tried sticking a single black hawk silhouette onto large windows to scare birds away. Wildlife researchers eventually discovered that this method rarely worked: birds simply flew around the sticker and struck the rest of the glass. What birds actually need is a subtle visual pattern spaced no more than a palm's width apart, signaling that (21).

Today, several cities encourage schools and offices to apply rows of tiny white ceramic dots or frosted stripes across exterior glass. From inside a classroom, people can still enjoy clear outdoor views almost unchanged, yet birds perceive a solid barrier from several meters away. Early trials at a lakeside high school showed that collisions dropped by over eighty percent in a single autumn, proving that (22).
passage.translation: 現代のオフィスビルや学校図書館には自然光を室内に取り込む大きなガラス窓が多く使われている。明るい室内は節電になり人間には快適だが、透明な大判ガラスは野鳥に思わぬ危険をもたらす。ガラスが周囲の木々や雲を鏡のように映すため、渡り鳥が開けた空と勘違いして衝突してしまうのだ。長年、建物管理者は鳥を遠ざけようと鷹の黒いシルエットのシールを1枚だけ大きな窓に貼ってきたが、鳥はシールを避けて残りのガラス面にぶつかるだけでほとんど効果がないことが研究で判明した。鳥が本当に必要としているのは手のひら幅以下の間隔で並んだ細かな視覚パターンであり、それによって(21)と伝わるのである。現在では複数の都市がガラス外側に小さな白い点や曇りガラス状の縞模様を貼ることを推奨している。教室内からの眺めはほぼ変わらない一方、鳥には数メートル手前から確かな障害物として認識される。湖畔の高校での試験ではひと秋で衝突が8割以上減少し、(22)ことが実証された。

items.explanation: 室内の明るい眺望をほとんど損なわずに衝突を80％以上減らせたことから、「小さな設計上の工夫で部屋を暗くせずに鳥を守れる」が結論として最も適切。

passage.title: Schedule and Costume Guide for the Autumn Choral Exchange
passage.text:
From: Clara Bennett, Regional Youth Choir Coordinator
To: Participating High School Choir Leaders
Subject: Next Saturday's joint concert at Civic Concert Hall

Dear choir leaders,
We are delighted that eight high school choirs will gather at Civic Concert Hall next Saturday, November 7, for our annual Autumn Choral Exchange. Please share the following final details with your members before Wednesday.

Although the public performance begins at 1:30 p.m., all choirs must check in at the north stage entrance between 9:45 a.m. and 10:15 a.m. Each school will have strictly twelve minutes on stage during the morning acoustic check, followed by a combined rehearsal of the closing song with all two hundred singers at 11:40 a.m.

Dressing rooms on the basement level are shared by two schools each, so please ask students not to bring large wheeled suitcases. Choirs may wear either their regular school uniforms or black-and-white concert attire; however, shoes with hard metal heels are prohibited by the hall manager because they scratch the cedar stage floor.

Finally, audience admission is free, and family members do not need tickets, though recording videos with tripods in the aisles is not allowed for fire-safety reasons. Let me know by Thursday evening if your pianist requires a page turner.

Warmly,
Clara Bennett
passage.translation: 差出人クララ・ベネット（地域青少年合唱コーディネーター）、宛先参加高校合唱部部長各位、件名：来週土曜の市民コンサートホール合同演奏会について。来週11月7日（土）の秋の合唱交流会に8校が集まることを嬉しく思う。水曜までに部員へ以下の最終連絡を共有してほしい。一般開演は午後1時30分だが、全校午前9時45分〜10時15分の間に北側楽屋口で受付を済ませること。午前の音響確認は1校あたり厳守で12分間ずつ行い、11時40分から200人全員でのフィナーレ合同練習を行う。地下の控室は2校ずつの相部屋となるため、大きなキャスター付きスーツケースの持ち込みは控えること。衣装は学校の制服または白黒の演奏会衣装のどちらでもよいが、杉材の舞台床を傷つけるため硬い金具付きヒールの靴はホール管理者により禁止されている。入場は無料で家族もチケット不要だが、防火安全上、通路に三脚を立てての動画撮影は禁止。伴奏者に譜めくり係が必要な場合は木曜夕方までに連絡すること。

items.prompt: Why are shoes with hard metal heels NOT allowed on stage?

They are slippery on the basement stairs.
items.explanation: 杉材のステージ床に傷をつけてしまう（scratch the cedar stage floor）ためホール管理者により禁止されている。
distractorReasons: ピアノ独奏中の音だけが理由ではない。
because they scratch the cedar stage floorと一致。
制服に合わないからではない。
地下階段で滑るからとは書かれていない。
items.translation: 硬い金具のついたヒールの靴がステージ上で禁止されているのはなぜですか。

items.prompt: Why does lending household tools make sense for people living in apartments?
choices: Apartment residents repair bookshelves every single day of the year.
Useful tools can be costly and take up scarce closet space when rarely used.
Hardware stores are no longer allowed to sell sewing machines.
Power tools work better inside library reading rooms.
items.explanation: 年に数回しか使わない道具を個別に買うのは高価であり、狭い集合住宅では収納場所も限られるため地域での共有が理にかなっている。
distractorReasons: 毎日修理するわけではなく残り364日は眠っているとある。
Buying decent equipment is expensive, and small apartments rarely have extra storage spaceと一致。
市販禁止になったわけではない。
閲覧室内で電動工具を使うわけではない。
items.translation: 集合住宅に暮らす人々にとって、家庭用の道具を借りられる仕組みが理にかなっているのはなぜですか。

passage.title: Why Public Libraries Are Lending Household Tools
passage.text:
When people think of a public library, they naturally picture rows of novels, study desks, and children's picture books. Over the past decade, however, dozens of municipal libraries have quietly added a very different section: shelves stocked with electric drills, sewing machines, hedge trimmers, and kitchen food dehydrators that residents can borrow with an ordinary library card.

The idea grew out of a simple observation about modern apartments. Many tools are essential for an occasional task, such as putting up a bookshelf, hemming curtains, or pruning a backyard tree, yet sit unused in closets for the other 364 days of the year. Buying decent equipment is expensive, and small apartments rarely have extra storage space. Sharing durable tools across a neighborhood reduces both household spending and manufacturing waste.

In the port city of Westhaven, the central library launched its "Tool Corner" three years ago with forty donated items inspected by retired electricians and carpenters. Before borrowing power tools for the first time, residents watch a five-minute safety video and sign an agreement promising to return items clean. A modest late fee encourages borrowers to bring popular items back on schedule so weekend projects are not delayed for the next person.

Interestingly, library staff noticed an unexpected benefit. Residents who visited initially to borrow a sewing machine or bicycle repair stand often left with craft manuals, gardening guides, or cookbooks as well, bringing first-time adult visitors into the building.

Running a tool library still requires dedicated space and regular maintenance checks, so not every small branch can store heavy garden equipment. Even so, Westhaven's experience shows that libraries have always been about sharing knowledge and practical resources that strengthen daily community life.
passage.translation: 公共図書館といえば小説の棚や自習机、児童絵本を思い浮かべるのが自然だが、ここ10年で多くの自治体図書館が電動ドリルやミシン、生垣バリカン、食品乾燥機などを通常の貸出カードで借りられるコーナーを設けている。背景には現代の住宅事情がある。本棚の設置やカーテンの裾上げ、庭木の剪定などに必要な道具も、年の残り364日は押し入れに眠ったままになりがちで、良質な器具は高価なうえ狭い集合住宅には収納場所も少ない。地域で丈夫な道具を共有すれば家計負担と製造廃棄物の双方を減らせる。港町ウェストヘイヴンの中央図書館では3年前、引退した電気技師や大工が点検した寄贈品40点で「ツール・コーナー」を開始した。初めて電動工具を借りる際は5分間の安全動画を見て、清掃して返却する同意書に署名する。少額の延滞料を設けることで週末の作業を待つ次の人のために期限通りの返却を促している。さらに思わぬ効果として、ミシンや自転車整備台を借りに来た住民が手芸書や園芸本、料理本も一緒に借りていくようになり、これまで来館しなかった大人の新規利用者が増えた。維持点検や保管場所が必要なため小さな分館すべてで大型園芸機器を扱えるわけではないが、図書館の本質が地域の暮らしを支える知識と実用資源の共有にあることを示している。

items.prompt: What must Westhaven residents do the first time they borrow a power tool?
choices: Donate two tools of their own to the central library.
Pass a two-hour written exam given by carpenters.
Pay half the retail price of the machine in cash.
Watch a short safety video and sign a clean-return agreement.
items.explanation: 初めて電動工具を借りる前には、5分間の安全動画を視聴し、きれいにして返却する旨の同意書に署名する必要がある。
distractorReasons: 2点の寄贈義務はない。
2時間の筆記試験はない。
定価の半額を払う必要はない（通常の貸出カードで借りられ延滞時のみ少額料金）。
watch a five-minute safety video and sign an agreement promising to return items cleanと一致。
items.translation: ウェストヘイヴンの住民が初めて電動工具を借りるときには何をしなければなりませんか。

passage.title: Why Public Libraries Are Lending Household Tools
passage.text:
When people think of a public library, they naturally picture rows of novels, study desks, and children's picture books. Over the past decade, however, dozens of municipal libraries have quietly added a very different section: shelves stocked with electric drills, sewing machines, hedge trimmers, and kitchen food dehydrators that residents can borrow with an ordinary library card.

The idea grew out of a simple observation about modern apartments. Many tools are essential for an occasional task, such as putting up a bookshelf, hemming curtains, or pruning a backyard tree, yet sit unused in closets for the other 364 days of the year. Buying decent equipment is expensive, and small apartments rarely have extra storage space. Sharing durable tools across a neighborhood reduces both household spending and manufacturing waste.

In the port city of Westhaven, the central library launched its "Tool Corner" three years ago with forty donated items inspected by retired electricians and carpenters. Before borrowing power tools for the first time, residents watch a five-minute safety video and sign an agreement promising to return items clean. A modest late fee encourages borrowers to bring popular items back on schedule so weekend projects are not delayed for the next person.

Interestingly, library staff noticed an unexpected benefit. Residents who visited initially to borrow a sewing machine or bicycle repair stand often left with craft manuals, gardening guides, or cookbooks as well, bringing first-time adult visitors into the building.

Running a tool library still requires dedicated space and regular maintenance checks, so not every small branch can store heavy garden equipment. Even so, Westhaven's experience shows that libraries have always been about sharing knowledge and practical resources that strengthen daily community life.

passage.text:
Hi!

Clara

items.model: Hi Clara, I am interested in becoming a pharmacist because helping patients understand their medicine safely is rewarding. Your career talk day sounds wonderful! How long did each speaker talk to the students? Also, could you ask questions after their speeches?
items.translation: こんにちは、クララ。私は患者さんが安全に薬を理解できるよう手助けすることにやりがいを感じるので、薬剤師になることに興味があります。キャリア講演会は素敵ですね！それぞれの講師はどのくらいの時間生徒たちに話しましたか。また、講演の後に質問をすることはできましたか。
items.explanation: Claraからの質問（興味のある仕事：薬剤師／魅力を感じる理由：患者の安全な服薬を支えるやりがい）に答えた上で、下線部のキャリア講演会について講演時間と質疑応答の有無を2つの疑問文で尋ねています（41語）。
rubric: 相手の質問（興味のある仕事とその理由）に明確に答えた
下線部（a career talk day）に関する具体的な質問を2つ書いた
時制（現在の関心と昨日の行事への質問）を正確に使い分けた
40〜50語の目安に収まっている

items.prompt:
次のQUESTIONについて、あなたの意見とその理由を2つ英文で書きなさい。（目安語数：50〜60語）
QUESTION: Do you think it is a good idea for high school students to join community volunteer activities on weekends?
items.model: I think it is a good idea for high school students to join community volunteer activities on weekends. First, working with people of different ages teaches students communication skills that they rarely practice in classrooms. Second, helping clean parks or run local events gives teenagers pride in their hometown and a stronger sense of responsibility.
items.translation: 私は高校生が週末に地域のボランティア活動に参加するのは良い考えだと思います。第一に、異なる世代の人々と協力することで、教室ではなかなか練習できないコミュニケーション力を学べます。第二に、公園の清掃や地域行事の運営を手伝うことは、十代の若者に地元への誇りとより強い責任感をもたらします。
items.explanation: 週末の地域ボランティア参加に賛成する立場を冒頭で示し、First（異世代との協働による対話力の向上）とSecond（清掃や行事運営を通じた郷土愛・責任感の育成）の2つの理由を55語で展開しています。
rubric: QUESTIONに対する賛否の立場を明確に示した
異世代交流・地域への責任感など異なる理由を2つ挙げた
動名詞主語や関係代名詞を用いて自然な英文で説明した
50〜60語の目安に収まっている

passage.title: Why Bakery Windows Fog Up Less Than Before
passage.text:
On cold winter mornings, small bakeries face a practical display problem. Warm steam rising from fresh trays of bread meets the icy glass of the front window and turns into tiny water droplets. While a misty window looks cozy in picture books, shop owners dislike it when passersby cannot see which breads have just come out of the oven.

Turning up the heater near the glass dries the window, yet dry hot air also makes uncovered croissants and crusty loaves lose moisture faster. A baker in Matsumoto found a simpler fix after talking with a neighbor who repaired eyeglasses. By installing a quiet ceiling fan that kept air moving gently across the glass and leaving a two-centimeter vent open near the top frame, the shop prevented warm damp air from sitting still against the cold pane. This adjustment (21) without drying out the bread.

Keeping the window clear had a welcome effect on morning sales. Commuters walking to the station could spot steaming walnut rolls from across the street and step inside on impulse. Sometimes solving an everyday shop problem requires (22) rather than buying a bigger heater.
passage.translation: 寒い冬の朝、小さなパン屋では焼きたてのパンの湯気が冷たい正面ガラスに触れて曇り、通行人からどのパンが焼き上がったか見えなくなる悩みがあります。ガラス近くの暖房を強めれば乾きますが、包装前のクロワッサンなどの水分まで奪ってしまいます。松本のパン職人は眼鏡修理をする隣人との会話からヒントを得て、静かな天井ファンでガラス面に緩やかな風を送り、上枠近くに2センチの通気口を開けて湿った暖かい空気が冷たいガラスに滞留しないようにしました。この工夫によりパンを乾燥させずに(21)ことができました。窓が澄んだままであることは朝の売上にも好影響を与え、駅へ向かう通勤客が通りの向こうから湯気の立つクルミパンを見つけて立ち寄るようになりました。日常の店の悩みは、大きな暖房機を買い足すより(22)ことで解決できる場合があります。

items.prompt: 空所(22)に入る最も適切なものを選んでください。
choices: closing the bakery during winter months

understanding how air and moisture move
replacing glass windows with brick walls

items.translation: 空所(22)の補充。

passage.title: Preparing Costumes for the Drama Festival
passage.text:
From: Ayaka Mori, Costume Team Leader
To: Drama Club Cast Members
Subject: Costume fittings and shoe rules this week

Hi everyone,
Our regional high school drama festival is two weeks away, and all jackets and skirts for our play have now been hemmed! Individual fifteen-minute fittings will take place in Clubroom 4 on Wednesday and Thursday after school. Please check the time chart taped to the clubroom door and come wearing the thin T-shirt and leggings you will wear under your costume.

During last Saturday's run-through, the wooden stage at Civic Hall turned out to be more slippery than our school gym floor. Because leather-soled shoes slide easily when turning quickly, our advisor has asked everyone to attach thin rubber grip pads to the bottoms of their stage shoes. Our costume team bought enough pads for the whole cast; bring your stage shoes to your fitting so we can put them on together.

After Thursday's fittings, all costumes will be packed into garment bags for transport. Please do not take any costume pieces home to wash, as household detergent may change the dye color of the matching jackets.

See you Wednesday,
Ayaka
passage.translation: 演劇部衣装班長の森アヤカから出演部員へのメール。地区高校演劇祭まであと2週間となり、全てのジャケットとスカートの裾上げが完了した。水曜と木曜の放課後に第4部室で1人15分の試着を行うので、部室扉の時間割を確認し、当日衣装の下に着る薄手のTシャツとレギンスを着用して来ること。先週土曜のリハーサルで市民ホールの木の舞台が学校の体育館より滑りやすいと判明したため、素早い回転で滑りやすい革底靴の裏に薄いゴムの滑り止めパッドを貼るよう顧問から指示があった。全員分のパッドを購入済みなので試着時に舞台靴を持参すること。木曜の試着後は運搬用の衣装袋に梱包するため、家庭用洗剤でお揃いのジャケットの色が変わるのを防ぐ目的で、自宅へ持ち帰って洗わないこと。

passage.title: Teaching Buses and Trains to Wait Two Minutes
passage.text:
Missing a rural connecting bus by ninety seconds can turn a twenty-minute commute into an hour-long wait on a windy platform. In large cities, where another train arrives every four minutes, tight transfers rarely matter. Along regional rail lines and suburban bus corridors, however, vehicles run far less frequently, so a single delayed train can strand dozens of passengers who needed that connection.

Historically, bus drivers had no reliable way to know whether an approaching train was running two minutes late or twenty. Waiting blindly risked making every downstream stop late and causing passengers further along the route to miss their own appointments. As a result, most operators instructed drivers to depart strictly by the printed clock, even if a train was just pulling into the station.

Low-cost GPS trackers and shared dispatch screens have begun changing this rigid rule. In several mid-sized European and Japanese cities, trains and connecting buses now exchange live location updates automatically. If a train is delayed by three minutes or less—and the bus schedule has enough cushion on a quiet stretch of road to make up that time—the screen on the driver's dashboard flashes a "hold" request. Meanwhile, an announcement inside the train tells transferring riders that their bus is waiting at Stand 2, preventing dangerous sprinting on station stairs.

Of course, holding a bus is not always wise. When heavy snow delays a train by fifteen minutes, holding every feeder bus would paralyze the entire local network. Dispatch software therefore sets clear upper limits, typically three to five minutes, and prioritizes the last evening runs when no later bus exists.

Passenger surveys in towns using smart-hold rules show a notable jump in trust toward public transit. Knowing that operators coordinate across vehicles makes people far more willing to leave their cars at home for two-seat journeys.
passage.translation: 地方で乗り継ぎバスを90秒差で逃すと、20分の移動が風の吹くホームでの1時間待ちに変わってしまいます。4分おきに次の電車が来る大都市とは異なり、本数の少ない地方鉄道や郊外バスでは、1本の遅れが多くの乗客を足止めします。以前はバスの運転手には電車が2分遅れなのか20分遅れなのか正確に知る手段がなく、当てずっぽうに待てば先の停留所すべてが遅れるため、電車がホームに入りかけていても時刻表どおり発車するのが一般的でした。しかし安価なGPS追跡装置と共有運行画面がこの硬直した運用を変え始めています。欧州や日本の中規模都市では鉄道と接続バスが位置情報を自動共有し、電車の遅れが3分程度でバスの走行区間に遅れを取り戻せる余裕があれば運転席画面に待機指示が出ます。車内放送でも2番乗り場でバスが待っていると伝わるため、駅の階段を危険に駆け下りる必要もなくなります。もちろん大雪で15分遅れた場合に全バスを止めれば路線網が麻痺するため、ソフトは通常3〜5分の上限を設け、最終便を優先します。導入した町では公共交通への信頼が高まり、乗り継ぎを伴う移動でもマイカーを控える人が増えています。

items.prompt: What benefit does the announcement inside the train provide?
choices: It tells riders to take a taxi instead.
It stops passengers from rushing dangerously down station stairs.
It lets passengers vote on the bus route.
items.explanation: バスが乗り場で待っていると車内で知らせることで、駅の階段を危険に走るのを防ぐ。
distractorReasons: コーヒー割引券ではない。
タクシー利用の指示ではない。
preventing dangerous sprinting on station stairsと一致。
ルート投票ではない。
items.translation: 電車内の案内放送にはどのような利点がありますか。

As a result, most operators instructed drivers to depart strictly by the printed clock, even if a train was just pulling into the station.

Low-cost GPS trackers and shared dispatch screens have begun changing this rigid rule. In several mid-sized European and Japanese cities, trains and connecting buses now exchange live location updates automatically. If a train is delayed by three minutes or less—and the bus schedule has enough cushion on a quiet stretch of road to make up that time—the screen on the driver's dashboard flashes a "hold" request. Meanwhile, an announcement inside the train tells transferring riders that their bus is waiting at Stand 2, preventing dangerous sprinting on station stairs.

Of course, holding a bus is not always wise. When heavy snow delays a train by fifteen minutes, holding every feeder bus would paralyze the entire local network. Dispatch software therefore sets clear upper limits, typically three to five minutes, and prioritizes the last evening runs when no later bus exists.

Passenger surveys in towns using smart-hold rules show a notable jump in trust toward public transit. Knowing that operators coordinate across vehicles makes people far more willing to leave their cars at home for two-seat journeys.

passage.title: Why Orchards Leave Strips of Wildflowers
passage.text:
Walk through a traditional fruit orchard, and you often see neatly mowed grass between every row of apple or pear trees. Tidy turf makes it easy to move ladders and harvest crates. In recent years, however, many fruit growers have stopped mowing the center of every lane, planting narrow strips of clover and native wildflowers instead.

The main reason is pollination and natural pest control. Fruit blossoms open for only a couple of weeks in spring. If an orchard offers no nectar for the rest of the year, wild bees and hoverflies move elsewhere. Wildflower strips bloom from April through October, keeping beneficial insects living right beside the trees. Ladybugs and lacewings sheltering in the flowers also feed on aphids, which helps farmers (21).

Growers still mow a clean path directly beneath the tree trunks so fallen fruit can be spotted and mice do not chew the bark in winter. Balancing neat working lanes with blooming strips shows that (22).
passage.translation: 従来の果樹園ではリンゴや梨の並木の間に短く刈り込まれた草が見られ、脚立や収穫箱を動かしやすくなっています。しかし近年は通路の中央を刈らず、クローバーや在来の野の花を細長く植える農家が増えています。主な理由は受粉と自然な害虫防除です。果樹の花が咲くのは春のわずか2週間ほどで、他の時期に蜜がなければ野生のハチやヒラタアブは別の場所へ移ってしまいます。野草帯は4月から10月まで咲き続けて益虫を木のそばに定住させ、花に潜むテントウムシやクサカゲロウがアブラムシを食べてくれるため農家は(21)ことができます。もっとも落果を見つけやすく冬にネズミが樹皮をかじらないよう幹の真下は今もきれいに刈られており、作業通路と花帯の両立は(22)ことを示しています。

passage.title: Borrowing Snowshoes for the Winter Nature Walk
passage.text:
From: Kogen Nature Center
To: Registered Participants
Subject: Footwear and arrival time for Sunday's snowshoe walk

Dear participants,
We look forward to welcoming you to Sunday's guided snowshoe walk through Shirakaba Woods. Light snow fell yesterday, leaving forty centimeters of fresh powder along the trail—ideal conditions for beginners!

If you reserved rental snowshoes on your application form, please arrive at the nature center by 9:10 a.m., twenty minutes before the walk starts, so staff can adjust the straps to fit your boots. Note that we rent only snowshoes, not winter boots. You must wear waterproof hiking boots or tall snow boots that cover your ankles; low sneakers allow snow inside and slip out of the bindings.

Walking on snow warms the body faster than people expect. Instead of one thick down coat, wear two or three breathable layers that you can unzip or put in your backpack during uphill sections. Hot herb tea will be served in the log cabin after we return at noon; bring your own insulated mug if you have one.

Warm regards,
Kogen Nature Center Staff
passage.translation: 高原ネイチャーセンターから登録参加者へのメール。日曜の白樺の森ガイド付きスノーシュー散策の案内。昨日の小雪でコースには初心者にも最適な40センチの新雪が積もっている。申込書でレンタルスノーシューを予約した人は、ストラップを靴に合わせるため開始20分前の午前9時10分までに到着すること。貸し出すのはスノーシューのみで冬用ブーツの貸出はないため、足首まで覆う防水トレッキング靴または長めのスノーブーツを履いてくること（丈の低いスニーカーは雪が入り留め具から外れる）。雪上歩行は想像以上に体が温まるため、厚手のダウン1枚ではなく登りでファスナーを開けたりリュックにしまったりできる重ね着を勧める。正午に帰着後ログキャビンで温かいハーブティーを振る舞うので、保温マグがあれば持参してほしい。

足首まで覆う防水ブーツ。
革靴ではない。

items.translation: 参加者は自分でどのような履物を履いていかなければなりませんか。

15分進めてあるとはない。
第2段落の2つの利点と一致。
広場を暖める機能はない。

passage.title: Why Public Clocks Still Matter in the Smartphone Era
passage.text:
Almost everyone walking through a train station plaza or town square today carries an exact atomic-synced clock in a coat pocket. At first glance, spending municipal money to maintain large analog clocks on towers, schools, and park posts might seem outdated. Yet when cities remove broken public clocks instead of repairing them, residents surprisingly often petition to bring them back.

One reason is practical convenience in moments when hands are occupied. A parent holding a toddler's hand, a cyclist waiting at an intersection, or a commuter carrying grocery bags in winter gloves can check a clock face in half a second without unzipping a pocket. Even more importantly, pulling out a smartphone just to check the time frequently leads to unintended distraction—one glance at a notification banner, and five minutes vanish.

Urban designers point to a subtler social role as well. Unlike a private screen, a public clock creates a shared reference point in physical space. Saying "Let's meet under the station clock at two" gives friends and visitors an unmistakable landmark visible from across a crowded square. During major power or cellular outages following storms, wind-up or battery-backed tower clocks have also continued marking time calmly when digital displays went dark.

Maintaining outdoor clocks does require skilled hands. Gears exposed to freezing rain, sea breeze, and nesting birds must be cleaned and lubricated regularly, and fewer young technicians train in turret clockwork today. To keep costs manageable, some towns pair modern solar-charged movements behind historic dial faces, preserving the familiar look while simplifying upkeep.

Far from being mere nostalgia, a well-placed town clock quietly supports punctual, unhurried movement through shared streets.
passage.translation: 今日、駅前広場や町の広場を歩くほぼすべての人がポケットに正確な時計（スマートフォン）を持っています。一見すると塔や学校、公園の大型アナログ時計を公費で維持するのは時代遅れに思えるかもしれませんが、壊れた時計を修理せず撤去すると住民から復活を求める声が驚くほど多く上がります。理由のひとつは手がふさがっている時の利便性で、幼児と手をつなぐ親や交差点で待つ自転車利用者、冬の手袋で買い物袋を持つ人も、ポケットを開けず0.5秒で時刻を確認できます。さらにスマホを取り出すと通知に気を取られて時間を奪われがちです。都市デザイナーは社会的な役割も指摘します。個人の画面と違い公共時計は空間の共有目印になり、「2時に駅の時計の下で」と迷わず待ち合わせでき、嵐による停電や通信障害時にもぜんまい式や電池バックアップの塔時計は時を刻み続けました。雨風や潮風、鳥の巣から歯車を守る保守技術者の減少に対し、歴史ある文字盤の裏に太陽光充電式ムーブメントを組み合わせる自治体もあります。公共時計は単なる懐古ではなく、街の暮らしを静かに支えています。

items.prompt: How do public clocks serve a social or emergency function according to the third paragraph?
choices: They count how many cyclists cross an intersection.
They broadcast loud music every fifteen minutes.
They charge commuters' phones wirelessly from across the square.
They act as clear meeting landmarks and can keep working during cellular or power outages.
items.explanation: 広場での分かりやすい待ち合わせの目印になり、停電や通信障害の際にも動き続けた例がある。
distractorReasons: 自転車の通行量計測ではない。
15分ごとの大音量音楽はない。
ワイヤレス充電の話はない。
第3段落の内容と一致。
items.translation: 第3段落によると、公共時計は社会的または非常時にどのような役割を果たしますか。

items.prompt: Heavy rain forced the staff to (     ) the fireworks show until next weekend.

pretendはふりをする。
preserveは保存する。
promoteは促進する。

items.prompt: This herbal hand cream is completely free (     ) artificial fragrances and dyes.

items.prompt: Before buying a secondhand bicycle, inspect the frame closely for any signs of (     ).

B: (     ) However, the Sunday morning slot on the same weekend is wide open.

B: (     ) I have a bottle of chain oil in our garage.
A: Really? I'd appreciate your help!
choices: You should throw the bike away.
Let's clean and oil it after school.

捨てるよう勧めるのはオイルがある話と矛盾。

I start my first shift next month.

choices: avoid reading any fiction published this century
memorize the barcode numbers of every shelf
finish every 500-page history book in ten minutes
discover titles they might never have picked up on their own
items.explanation: 店員個人の率直な紹介と好みの相性によって、自分ひとりでは手に取らなかったような本に出会える。

バーコード暗記ではない。
10分で読破できるわけではない。
第2段落の案内機能と最終段落のan overlooked novelにつながる。

passage.title: Why Bookstores Write Hand-Lettered Shelf Cards
passage.text:
Online bookshops can display thousands of customer star ratings on a single screen, yet independent neighborhood bookstores continue to rely on something far simpler: small paper cards taped beneath shelves, written by hand by staff members. At first, spending hours writing individual notes with felt pens might seem inefficient when printed summaries already appear on every back cover.

Back-cover blurbs, however, are written to make every book sound equally thrilling. Readers browsing a quiet shop often want a more honest guide—why this particular mystery suits a rainy Sunday, or which history book explains a complex era without heavy jargon. Because each card carries the staff writer's first name, regular customers soon learn whose taste matches their own. This personal voice helps browsers (21).

Staff members say writing the cards changes how they read as well. Paying attention to who might enjoy an overlooked novel turns stocking shelves from routine labor into (22). Even in a digital age, a three-sentence note from a trusted human reader still moves books off the shelf.
passage.translation: ネット書店は画面に何千件もの星評価を表示できますが、街の独立系書店は今も店員が手書きした小さな棚カード（ポップ）を大切にしています。裏表紙に印刷されたあらすじがあるのに何時間もかけて手書きするのは一見非効率に思えるかもしれません。しかし裏表紙の宣伝文はどの本も同じように魅力的に見せるためのもので、静かな店内を歩く読者が求めているのは「なぜこの推理小説が雨の日曜に合うのか」「専門用語なしで読める歴史書はどれか」といった率直な案内です。カードには書いた店員の名前が入っているため、常連客は誰の好みが自分と合うか自然と分かり、この肉声の案内が来店客に(21)助けとなります。店員側も、埋もれがちな小説を誰が好きそうか意識して読むようになり、棚出し作業が単なる作業から(22)へと変わると話します。デジタル時代でも信頼できる読み手の3文のメモが本を動かしています。

items.prompt: 空所(22)に入る最も適切なものを選んでください。
choices: a thoughtful conversation with the neighborhood
a reason to remove all chairs from the store
an excuse to stop ordering new books
a contest over who has the smallest handwriting
items.explanation: 単調な棚補充を「地域の読者との心のこもった対話」へと変える。
distractorReasons: routine laborとの対比として最も自然。
椅子を撤去する理由ではない。
新刊発注をやめる口実ではない。
文字の小ささ競争ではない。
items.translation: 空所(22)の補充。

passage.title: Instructions for the Astronomical Choir Recording
passage.text:
From: Mr. Shinohara, Chorus Club Director
To: Chorus Club Members
Subject: Sunday's recording session in the civic auditorium

Dear members,
This Sunday afternoon, a local radio technician will record two of our songs in the civic auditorium for the winter youth music broadcast. Because the auditorium's microphones are sensitive enough to pick up rustling cloth and clicking jewelry, please wear soft cotton shirts without zippers, metal buttons, or bracelets.

We will enter through the backstage door on the west side at 1:15 p.m.; the front glass doors will stay locked because no audience is attending. Warm-up exercises begin at 1:30 p.m., and recording runs from 2:15 p.m. to 3:45 p.m.

Cold winter air dries vocal cords quickly, so bring a bottle of plain room-temperature water. Please avoid milk tea or sweet juice right before singing, as sugar and dairy can coat your throat and make clear high notes harder. Cough drops may be used during breaks, not while standing on the risers.

Let's enjoy making a recording we'll remember!
Mr. Shinohara
passage.translation: 合唱部顧問の篠原先生から部員へのメール。今週日曜午後、冬の青少年音楽放送向けに地元ラジオ局の技術者が市民会館の大ホールで2曲を録音してくれる。ホールのマイクは非常に高感度で衣擦れやアクセサリーのカチカチ音まで拾ってしまうため、ファスナーや金属ボタンのない柔らかい綿のシャツを着て、ブレスレットは外してくること。観客は入らないため正面ガラス扉は施錠されており、午後1時15分に西側の楽屋口から入館する。1時30分から発声練習、2時15分〜3時45分に録音を行う。冬の乾いた空気で声帯が乾きやすいため常温の水を持参すること。砂糖や乳製品は喉に膜を作って高音が出にくくなるため、歌う直前のミルクティーや甘いジュースは控えること。のど飴はひな壇の上ではなく休憩中に舐めること。

items.prompt: How will club members enter the civic auditorium on Sunday?
choices: Through the front glass doors at 2:15 p.m.
Through the west backstage door at 1:15 p.m.
With audience ticket holders at noon.
items.explanation: We will enter through the backstage door on the west side at 1:15 p.m.とある。
distractorReasons: 正面ガラス扉は施錠されたまま。
地下改札ではない。
午後1時15分に西側の楽屋口から入る。
無観客で行うため観客はいない。
items.translation: 日曜日に部員たちはどのように市民会館へ入りますか。

We will enter through the backstage door on the west side at 1:15 p.m.; the front glass doors will stay locked because no audience is attending. Warm-up exercises begin at 1:30 p.m., and recording runs from 2:15 p.m. to 3:45 p.m.

Cold winter air dries vocal cords quickly, so bring a bottle of plain room-temperature water. Please avoid milk tea or sweet juice right before singing, as sugar and dairy can coat your throat and make clear high notes harder. Let's enjoy making a recording we'll remember!
Mr. Shinohara
passage.translation: 合唱部顧問の篠原先生から部員へのメール。今週日曜午後、冬の青少年音楽放送向けに地元ラジオ局の技術者が市民会館の大ホールで2曲を録音してくれる。ホールのマイクは非常に高感度で衣擦れやアクセサリーのカチカチ音まで拾ってしまうため、ファスナーや金属ボタンのない柔らかい綿のシャツを着て、ブレスレットは外してくること。観客は入らないため正面ガラス扉は施錠されており、午後1時15分に西側の楽屋口から入館する。1時30分から発声練習、2時15分〜3時45分に録音を行う。冬の乾いた空気で声帯が乾きやすいため常温の水を持参すること。砂糖や乳製品は喉に膜を作って高音が出にくくなるため、歌う直前のミルクティーや甘いジュースは控えること。のど飴はひな壇の上ではなく休憩中に舐めること。

passage.title: How Curved Sidewalk Corners Shape Street Safety
passage.text:
Most pedestrians never think twice about the shape of a street corner where two sidewalks meet. Yet traffic engineers know that the radius of that curve—whether it forms a sharp ninety-degree turn or a wide, sweeping arc—has a direct effect on how fast cars turn and how safely people cross.

During the mid-twentieth century, many cities widened intersection corners into gentle curves so large trucks and buses could turn without slowing down much. While convenient for vehicles, wide curves had two drawbacks for walkers. First, drivers could swing around corners at twenty-five or thirty kilometers per hour while looking mainly for oncoming cars rather than people in the crosswalk. Second, rounding off the corner pushed the curb back, making the painted crosswalk several meters longer for children and older residents to cross.

In recent years, urban planners have been tightening residential and school-zone corners again. A tighter curb forces passenger cars to slow to walking pace before turning, giving drivers an extra second or two to spot someone stepping off the sidewalk. Extending the corner slightly—a design often called a "curb bulb"—also shortens the crossing distance and lets pedestrians see past parked cars without stepping into traffic.

What about fire engines and delivery trucks that still need room to turn? Engineers solve this in creative ways. On some corners, they build a low, textured stone apron beside the curb: ordinary cars stay off the bumpy surface, while the wide wheels of an emergency vehicle can roll slowly over it when necessary.

Small geometric changes in concrete rarely make headlines, yet reshaping a single corner can calm an entire neighborhood crossing every day of the year.
passage.translation: 2本の歩道が交わる街角の形を普段意識する歩行者はほとんどいませんが、その角の丸み（急な直角に近いか、大きく緩やかな弧か）は車の右左折速度と横断の安全性に直結します。20世紀半ばには大型トラックやバスが減速せずに曲がれるよう角を大きく丸める設計が広がりましたが、歩行者には2つの欠点がありました。運転手が時速25〜30キロのまま対向車ばかり見て曲がれてしまうことと、縁石が後退して子どもや高齢者が渡る横断歩道が数メートル長くなることです。近年、住宅街や通学路では再び角を小さく引き締める改修が進んでいます。乗用車は歩くような速度まで落として曲がることになり歩行者を見つける余裕が生まれ、「カーブバルブ（歩道張り出し）」によって横断距離が縮まり駐車車両の陰からも見通しが良くなります。消防車や配送トラックの回転スペースについては、乗用車は避けるが大型緊急車両は必要時にゆっくり乗り上げられる段差の低い石畳エプロンを設けるなどの工夫で解決しています。小さな形の工夫が毎日の交差点の安全を支えています。

横断歩道内駐車を認めるのではない。

items.translation: 「カーブバルブ（歩道の張り出し）」は道路を渡る人をどのように助けますか。

passage.title: Why Libraries Lend Sewing Machines and Tools
passage.text:
For generations, people thought of public libraries solely as quiet halls lined with books, magazines, and newspapers. Over the past decade, however, dozens of municipal libraries have added an unexpected shelf near the checkout counter—one stocked with sewing machines, pruning shears, air-quality monitors, and cake pans.

The idea behind a "library of things" is straightforward. Many household tools are genuinely useful twice a year, yet sit gathering dust in a closet for the other fifty weeks. Buying a decent sewing machine just to hem two pairs of curtains is expensive, especially for students or young families living in compact apartments with little storage space. Borrowing equipment with an ordinary library card lets residents (21).

Sharing infrequent tools brings community benefits as well. Librarians often pair popular items with beginner workshops led by retired tailors or carpenters, turning solitary repairs into friendly learning sessions. In this way, lending practical tools extends a library's traditional mission: giving everyone equal access to (22) regardless of income.
passage.translation: 何世代もの間、公共図書館といえば本や雑誌、新聞が並ぶ静かな場所だと考えられてきました。しかしこの10年ほどの間に、多くの市立図書館が貸出カウンターの近くにミシン、剪定ばさみ、空気質計、ケーキ型などを備えた意外な棚を設けるようになっています。「モノの図書館」の発想は明快です。家庭用の道具には年に2回は本当に役立つものの、残りの50週間は押し入れでほこりをかぶるものが少なくありません。カーテン2組の裾上げのためだけに立派なミシンを買うのは高くつき、収納の限られた集合住宅に暮らす学生や若い世帯にはなおさら負担です。普段の図書カードで道具を借りられれば住民は(21)ことができます。また、退職した仕立て職人や大工による初心者講座と組み合わせることで孤立しがちな修繕作業が温かい学びの場にもなり、実用道具の貸出は所得にかかわらず誰にでも(22)への平等なアクセスを届けるという図書館本来の使命を広げています。

passage.title: Instructions for Saturday's Coastal Bird Count
passage.text:
From: Minato Wild Bird Society
To: Student Volunteers
Subject: Checklist for Saturday's winter waterfowl survey

Dear student volunteers,
Thank you for signing up to assist with our annual winter waterfowl count along Minato Bay this Saturday morning. Data collected by teams like yours over the past thirty years helps biologists track how duck and gull populations respond to warmer winters.

We will meet at the Observation Pier parking lot at 7:20 a.m. Because bright red, yellow, or white jackets startle resting flocks from far away, please wear muted colors such as olive green, brown, gray, or navy blue. Binoculars and waterproof tally sheets will be lent to each pair at registration.

Counting three hundred ducks bobbing on waves takes practice! Don't worry about getting an exact single-digit figure on your first try—an experienced leader will walk with every pair and show you how to count birds in groups of ten.

Warmly,
Keiichi Sato, Survey Coordinator
passage.translation: みなと野鳥の会の調査担当・佐藤圭一から高校生ボランティアへのメール。今週土曜午前の毎年恒例・みなと湾冬季水鳥調査への参加に感謝する。過去30年にわたり集められたデータは、暖冬に対するカモやカモメの個体数変化を追跡するのに役立っている。午前7時20分に展望桟橋の駐車場に集合。鮮やかな赤・黄・白の上着は遠くからでも休んでいる群れを驚かせてしまうため、オリーブ色・茶・灰・紺など落ち着いた色の服を着てくること。双眼鏡と防水記録用紙は受付で各ペアに貸し出す。波に揺れる300羽のカモを数えるには慣れが要るため、最初から1羽単位で完璧に数えようと心配しなくて大丈夫で、経験豊富なリーダーが各ペアに同行し10羽単位で数えるコツを教えてくれる。

items.explanation: Binoculars and waterproof tally sheets will be lent to each pair at registration.とある。
distractorReasons: 双眼鏡と防水の集計用紙。
カメラではない。

ゴムボートではない。
items.translation: 受付で各ペアに貸し出される物は何ですか。

items.prompt: Why do leafy vegetables like spinach wilt quickly in dry store air?

passage.title: Why Supermarkets Mist Vegetables Gently—and Leave Others Dry
passage.text:
Shoppers reaching for lettuce or broccoli in the produce aisle often hear a soft rumble of thunder from hidden speakers just before fine water droplets drift over the greens. Although the sound effect is playful, the misting system itself serves a practical purpose grounded in plant biology.

Even after harvest, leafy vegetables such as spinach, kale, and parsley continue losing moisture through microscopic pores on their leaves. Because these greens have a large surface area and very thin outer skins, dry store air can leave them limp within hours, forcing grocers to throw away otherwise nutritious food. Periodic bursts of cool mist keep humidity high around the leaves and slow down wilting, while the brief sound warning lets customers step back so their sleeves stay dry.

Not every vegetable benefits from a shower, however. Onions, garlic, potatoes, and winter squash are stored in dry bins far from the mist nozzles. Evolved as underground bulbs or thick-skinned storage organs, these crops naturally resist drying out; getting them wet in a warm store actually encourages mold and premature sprouting. Tomatoes and mushrooms likewise spoil faster when damp.

In recent years, several grocery chains have replaced open misting with ultrasonic humidifiers that create fog droplets too tiny to wet surfaces. Because excess water no longer pools at the bottom of display trays, stores report less bacterial rot and longer shelf life.

Knowing how different vegetables respond to moisture helps shoppers at home too: leafy greens stay crisp wrapped in a slightly damp cloth in the fridge, whereas onions belong in a cool, dry basket.
passage.translation: 青果売り場でレタスやブロッコリーに手を伸ばすと、小さな雷鳴の効果音の直後に細かい霧が葉物野菜に降り注ぐことがあります。収穫後もホウレンソウやパセリなどの葉物野菜は葉の微細な気孔から水分を失い続け、表面積が大きく表皮が薄いため店内の乾いた空気で数時間のうちにしおれて廃棄につながります。定期的な冷たいミストは葉の周囲の湿度を高く保ってしおれを遅らせ、事前の音は買い物客の袖が濡れないよう知らせる役割を果たします。一方でタマネギ、ニンニク、ジャガイモ、カボチャなどは乾燥した棚に置かれます。これらは地中の鱗茎や厚い皮を持つ貯蔵器官として進化しており乾燥に強く、暖かい店内で濡らすとカビや発芽を招いてしまいます。トマトやキノコも湿ると傷みやすくなります。近年は表面を濡らさないほど微細な霧を出す超音波加湿器に切り替える店も増え、トレイの底に水がたまらないため腐敗が減っています。この違いを知れば家庭でも葉物は少し湿らせた布で冷蔵庫へ、タマネギは涼しく乾いたかごへと適切に保存できます。

passage.title: Why Supermarkets Mist Vegetables Gently—and Leave Others Dry
passage.text:
Shoppers reaching for lettuce or broccoli in the produce aisle often hear a soft rumble of thunder from hidden speakers just before fine water droplets drift over the greens. Although the sound effect is playful, the misting system itself serves a practical purpose grounded in plant biology.

Even after harvest, leafy vegetables such as spinach, kale, and parsley continue losing moisture through microscopic pores on their leaves. Because these greens have a large surface area and very thin outer skins, dry store air can leave them limp within hours, forcing grocers to throw away otherwise nutritious food. Periodic bursts of cool mist keep humidity high around the leaves and slow down wilting, while the brief sound warning lets customers step back so their sleeves stay dry.

Not every vegetable benefits from a shower, however. Onions, garlic, potatoes, and winter squash are stored in dry bins far from the mist nozzles. Evolved as underground bulbs or thick-skinned storage organs, these crops naturally resist drying out; getting them wet in a warm store actually encourages mold and premature sprouting. Tomatoes and mushrooms likewise spoil faster when damp.

In recent years, several grocery chains have replaced open misting with ultrasonic humidifiers that create fog droplets too tiny to wet surfaces. Because excess water no longer pools at the bottom of display trays, stores report less bacterial rot and longer shelf life.

Knowing how different vegetables respond to moisture helps shoppers at home too: leafy greens stay crisp wrapped in a slightly damp cloth in the fridge, whereas onions belong in a cool, dry basket.
passage.translation: 青果売り場でレタスやブロッコリーに手を伸ばすと、小さな雷鳴の効果音の直後に細かい霧が葉物野菜に降り注ぐことがあります。収穫後もホウレンソウやパセリなどの葉物野菜は葉の微細な気孔から水分を失い続け、表面積が大きく表皮が薄いため店内の乾いた空気で数時間のうちにしおれて廃棄につながります。定期的な冷たいミストは葉の周囲の湿度を高く保ってしおれを遅らせ、事前の音は買い物客の袖が濡れないよう知らせる役割を果たします。一方でタマネギ、ニンニク、ジャガイモ、カボチャなどは乾燥した棚に置かれます。これらは地中の鱗茎や厚い皮を持つ貯蔵器官として進化しており乾燥に強く、暖かい店内で濡らすとカビや発芽を招いてしまいます。トマトやキノコも湿ると傷みやすくなります。近年は表面を濡らさないほど微細な霧を出す超音波加湿器に切り替える店も増え、トレイの底に水がたまらないため腐敗が減っています。この違いを知れば家庭でも葉物は少し湿らせた布で冷蔵庫へ、タマネギは涼しく乾いたかごへと適切に保存できます。

passage.title: Why Stadium Grass Needs Artificial Sunlight
passage.text:
Modern soccer stadiums are built with steep, covered stands that shelter tens of thousands of fans from rain and wind, while keeping cheers echoing loudly around the pitch. For the groundskeepers tending the natural grass field, however, those towering roofs create a stubborn problem: even at noon on a sunny day, large sections of turf remain in deep shadow.

Grass blades need sunlight for photosynthesis, especially in winter when matches tear up wet soil and natural daylight hours are short. Without enough light, shaded goal areas quickly turn muddy and bare. To keep the turf thick and safe for players' ankles, many stadiums wheel out wide aluminum rigs fitted with high-efficiency grow lamps between matches. Sensors in the soil measure temperature and moisture so lamps warm and illuminate only the weakest patches. This targeted care (21).

Although running grow rigs uses electricity, keeping natural turf healthy avoids costly mid-season resodding, where entire truckloads of grass must be stripped and replaced. Healthy roots hold the ground together, proving that great stadium architecture must consider (22) as carefully as spectator comfort.
passage.translation: 現代のサッカースタジアムは数万人の観客を雨風から守り歓声を響かせるため、急勾配の屋根付きスタンドを備えています。しかし天然芝を管理するキーパーにとって高い屋根は厄介な問題を生みます。晴れた日の正午でさえピッチの広い範囲が濃い日陰になってしまうのです。特に雨で芝が傷み日照時間も短い冬場、光合成に必要な光が足りないとゴール前はすぐ泥だらけになってしまいます。選手の足首に安全な密な芝を保つため、多くのスタジアムでは試合の合間に高効率育成ランプを備えた大型照明装置を芝生の上に移動させ、土壌センサーで温度と水分を測りながら弱った箇所だけを照らします。この的確なケアによって(21)のです。電力は使うものの、シーズン途中にトラック何台分もの芝を張り替える莫大な費用を防げるため、優れたスタジアム設計には観客の快適さと同じくらい(22)への配慮が欠かせません。

自宅で作った生地の持ち込みは禁止。
20種のチーズではない。
items.translation: 決勝進出チームはレシピに必ず何を入れなければなりませんか。

passage.title: Guidelines for the High School Baking Contest
passage.text:
From: Prefectural Milk & Grain Council
To: Finalist Teams
Subject: Ingredient rules and oven slots for next Sunday's finals

Congratulations again on advancing to the six-team final of the High School Local Ingredient Baking Contest! Next Sunday's bake-off will take place in the Culinary Training Hall from 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.

Each team will have ninety minutes to bake twelve identical rolls or pastries featuring at least one fruit or vegetable grown in our prefecture. All dry ingredients must be weighed in the hall after the start signal; bringing pre-mixed dough from home is against the rules. However, fruit compotes or roasted sweet-potato fillings that require long simmering may be prepared the day before and brought in a sealed cooler box.

Because six teams share four large convection ovens, oven slots are staggered every ten minutes. Your team's assigned baking window is printed on the badge you will receive at 9:30 a.m. check-in.

Good luck to all bakers!
Contest Secretariat

Decorating the plates in the Culinary Training Hall.

長時間加熱を要するコンポートや焼き芋あんの前日調理・保冷持参は認められている。
粉類の計量は開始合図後に会場で行う。
前日の会場盛り付けではない。
items.translation: 前日に済ませておくことが認められている準備はどれですか。
