passage.title: A Space for the River
passage.text:
For many years, the people of Bellford regarded their river mainly as a threat. High walls separated it from nearby streets, and a narrow channel carried water quickly through the center of town. The design had protected buildings during many ordinary storms. However, as the town expanded, more roofs and paved surfaces prevented rain from soaking into the ground. Water reached the river faster, and maintaining safety became increasingly difficult.

One response would have been to make the walls higher. Instead, planners proposed allowing the river more room at a former industrial site upstream. Old warehouses there had been removed, leaving land that could temporarily hold water during heavy rain. In dry weather, most of the area could be used as a public park. The proposal did not eliminate the need for walls elsewhere; it was intended to complement existing defenses.

Some residents objected that a park designed to flood was a waste of money. They feared that equipment would be damaged and the area would be closed too often. The design team responded by placing expensive electrical equipment above expected water levels and choosing surfaces that could be cleaned after flooding. Path signs explained that lower routes might close, while a higher route would remain available under most conditions.

A more difficult question concerned who would benefit. The park was near a neighborhood with few green spaces, but many people living there had not attended the early planning meetings. The meetings had been held during working hours and relied on technical presentations. The town changed the schedule and used a temporary model that residents could walk around. This led to requests for better lighting, places to sit, and a safer crossing to the park.

After the park opened, a severe storm tested the design. Water spread across the lower ground as intended, and some paths were closed for cleaning afterward. Officials resisted describing this as a failure of the park: temporary flooding was part of its protective function. At the same time, they acknowledged that the cleanup had taken longer than expected and revised the maintenance plan.

Bellford's experience illustrates why adapting to floods involves more than building a single structure. The physical design, the ability to maintain it, and the ways people understand and use it all matter. A project can serve several purposes, but those purposes need to be explained honestly. Calling a floodable park permanently dry would create false expectations; treating it only as empty storage would overlook its everyday value to residents.
passage.translation: ベルフォードでは高い壁と狭い水路で川を制御してきましたが、市街化で雨水の地下浸透が減り、流入が速くなって安全確保が難しくなりました。壁を高くする代わりに、上流の旧工業用地を大雨時の貯水空間にし、通常は公園として使う案が出ました。既存の防御をなくすのでなく補完する計画です。設備の損傷や閉鎖への懸念には、電気設備の高所設置や清掃しやすい舗装、低い道の閉鎖表示と高い道の確保で対応しました。緑地の少ない近隣住民が初期会合に少なかったのは、勤務時間中の開催と技術的説明が原因でした。時間変更と歩いて見られる模型により、照明、椅子、安全な横断路の希望が集まりました。開園後の大雨では計画どおり低地に水が広がり、その後清掃のため道が閉じられました。行政は洪水自体を失敗とはしませんでしたが、清掃に想定以上の時間がかかったことは認め管理計画を改めました。物理的設計、維持能力、住民の理解と利用がいずれも重要です。多目的な施設の目的を正直に説明すべきで、常に乾燥した公園と呼ぶのも、単なる空の貯水場と見るのも適切ではありません。

choices: Replace every wall throughout the town.
Add temporary water storage while offering everyday public space.
Prevent all water from ever reaching the river.
Return the former warehouses to industrial use.
items.explanation: 大雨時は貯水、平常時は公園で既存防御を補完する。
distractorReasons: ほかの壁を不要にするのでない。
二重の用途と補完関係を正しくまとめる。
全雨水の流入防止ではない。
倉庫は除去済みで工業利用に戻さない。
items.translation: 新しい公園の役割は何ですか。

passage.title: A Space for the River
passage.text:
For many years, the people of Bellford regarded their river mainly as a threat. High walls separated it from nearby streets, and a narrow channel carried water quickly through the center of town. The design had protected buildings during many ordinary storms. However, as the town expanded, more roofs and paved surfaces prevented rain from soaking into the ground. Water reached the river faster, and maintaining safety became increasingly difficult.

One response would have been to make the walls higher. Instead, planners proposed allowing the river more room at a former industrial site upstream. Old warehouses there had been removed, leaving land that could temporarily hold water during heavy rain. In dry weather, most of the area could be used as a public park. The proposal did not eliminate the need for walls elsewhere; it was intended to complement existing defenses.

Some residents objected that a park designed to flood was a waste of money. They feared that equipment would be damaged and the area would be closed too often. The design team responded by placing expensive electrical equipment above expected water levels and choosing surfaces that could be cleaned after flooding. Path signs explained that lower routes might close, while a higher route would remain available under most conditions.

A more difficult question concerned who would benefit. The park was near a neighborhood with few green spaces, but many people living there had not attended the early planning meetings. The meetings had been held during working hours and relied on technical presentations. The town changed the schedule and used a temporary model that residents could walk around. This led to requests for better lighting, places to sit, and a safer crossing to the park.

After the park opened, a severe storm tested the design. Water spread across the lower ground as intended, and some paths were closed for cleaning afterward. Officials resisted describing this as a failure of the park: temporary flooding was part of its protective function. At the same time, they acknowledged that the cleanup had taken longer than expected and revised the maintenance plan.

Bellford's experience illustrates why adapting to floods involves more than building a single structure. The physical design, the ability to maintain it, and the ways people understand and use it all matter. A project can serve several purposes, but those purposes need to be explained honestly. Calling a floodable park permanently dry would create false expectations; treating it only as empty storage would overlook its everyday value to residents.

items.prompt: How did officials respond after the severe storm?

They closed the park permanently because water entered it.

items.prompt: Which statement best expresses the article's conclusion?
choices: Successful adaptation requires design, maintenance, participation, and honest explanation of functions.
A floodable park is useful only when it contains no visitors.
Technical structures make public understanding unnecessary.
Projects serving more than one purpose should always be rejected.

日常の住民への価値を認めている。
理解も重要と明記。
多目的性自体は否定していない。
items.translation: 本文の結論に最も近いものはどれですか。

items.prompt: 以下の英文を読んで、その内容を英語で要約し、解答欄に記入しなさい。本文にない自分の意見は加えないこと。（目安語数：45〜55語）

passage.title: Rethinking Nighttime Park Lighting
passage.text:
Many cities keep public parks brightly lit throughout the night. Strong white lights help pedestrians see walking paths clearly, give evening commuters a greater sense of security, and deter criminal behavior.

In recent years, however, researchers have pointed out the drawbacks of excessive nighttime lighting. Leaving powerful lamps on until morning consumes large amounts of electricity. In addition, artificial glare disrupts nocturnal insects and confuses migrating birds that rely on natural darkness.

To address these concerns without sacrificing public safety, several municipalities have redesigned their lighting systems. They now install shields that direct light downward onto paths and use motion sensors to dim lamps when nobody is nearby, protecting local ecosystems while saving energy.
passage.translation:
多くの都市では公共の公園を一晩中明るく照らしている。強い白色光は歩行者が歩道をはっきりと見られるようにし、夜間の通行人に安心感を与え、犯罪行為を抑止する。
しかし近年、研究者たちは過度な夜間照明の欠点を指摘している。強力な街灯を朝まで点灯し続けることは大量の電力を消費する。さらに人工的なまぶしさは夜行性の昆虫に悪影響を与え、自然の暗闇に頼る渡り鳥を混乱させる。
公共の安全を損なわずにこれらの懸念へ対処するため、複数の自治体が照明設備を再設計している。光を歩道へ下向きに絞るカバーを取り付け、近くに人がいないときは人感センサーで減光することで、電力を節約しつつ地域の生態系を守っている。

items.model: Bright park lighting at night helps pedestrians walk safely and prevents crime. However, excessive illumination consumes substantial electricity and harms nocturnal insects and migrating birds. Consequently, several cities now use downward-facing shields and motion sensors to conserve energy and protect wildlife while maintaining public safety.
items.translation: 夜間の明るい公園照明は歩行者の安全な通行を助け犯罪を防ぐ。しかし過度な照明は大量の電力を消費し、夜行性の昆虫や渡り鳥に害を与える。そのため複数の都市では現在、下向きカバーと人感センサーを用い、公共の安全を保ちながら節電と野生生物の保護を図っている。
items.explanation: 第1段落の利点（歩行者の安全・防犯）、第2段落の課題（電力消費と昆虫・渡り鳥への悪影響）、第3段落の解決策（下向き遮光カバーと人感センサーによる安全・節電・生態系保護の両立）を45語で端的にまとめています。
rubric: 夜間照明の利点（歩行者の安全・防犯）を簡潔に示した
過度な照明の欠点（電力消費・野生生物への悪影響）を含めた
自治体の改善策（下向き照明・人感センサー）と効果を結んだ
原文の表現を適切に言い換え45〜55語の目安に収めた

items.prompt:
次のTOPICについて、あなたの意見とその理由を2つ書きなさい。POINTSは理由を書く際の参考として自由に用いてかまいません。（目安語数：80〜100語）
TOPIC: Some people say that companies should encourage employees to take longer summer vacations. What do you think about that?
POINTS:
• Health
• Productivity
• Teamwork
items.model:
I agree that companies should encourage employees to take longer summer vacations.
First, extended rest protects workers' physical and mental health. Working continuously under heavy pressure often leads to exhaustion, whereas spending a full week away from office duties allows employees to recover completely.
Second, longer vacations can improve workplace productivity and teamwork. When employees return refreshed, they concentrate better and generate creative ideas. Moreover, sharing duties while colleagues are away helps teams organize tasks more systematically.
Therefore, promoting longer summer holidays benefits both employees and companies.
items.translation:
私は企業が従業員により長い夏季休暇を取るよう促すべきだという意見に賛成です。
第一に、まとまった休養は働く人の心身の健康を守ります。強い重圧の下で働き続けると疲労につながりやすいですが、職場の業務から丸1週間離れることで完全に回復できます。
第二に、長期休暇は職場の生産性とチームワークを高められます。リフレッシュして復帰すれば集中力が増し創造的な発想が生まれます。さらに同僚の不在中に業務を分担することで、チームはより体系的に仕事を整理できるようになります。
したがって、長い夏休みの推進は従業員と企業の双方に利益をもたらします。
items.explanation: 序論（賛成表明）→本論1（Health：継続勤務による疲労の防止と心身の回復）→本論2（Productivity / Teamwork：復帰後の集中力・創造性向上と業務分担の整理）→結論の4段落構成で87語にまとめています。
rubric: 序論・本論（理由2つ）・結論の明確な段落構成で書いた
2つの理由が互いに重複せず具体的に展開されている
適切な接続表現（First, whereas, Moreover, Therefore等）を用いた
80〜100語の目安に収まっている

items.prompt: The town council voted to (     ) the old harbour warehouse rather than demolish it.
items.explanation: 取り壊す（demolish）のではなく古い港の倉庫を「改修・修復する」ことに決めたのでrenovate。
distractorReasons: renovateは「建物を改修・刷新する」。
abandonは「放棄する」。
deceiveは「だます」。
scatterは「まき散らす」。
items.translation: 町議会は古い港の倉庫を取り壊すのではなく改修することを可決しました。

items.prompt: All visitors to the laboratory must obtain prior (     ) from the safety director.
items.explanation: 研究所への訪問者が安全管理者から事前に得なければならない「許可・承認」なのでauthorization。
distractorReasons: illusionは「幻想・錯覚」。
extinctionは「絶滅」。
prior authorizationで「事前の承認・許可」。
frustrationは「欲求不満」。
items.translation: 研究所への訪問者は全員、安全責任者から事前の承認を得なければなりません。

items.prompt: Because rainfall has been unusually scarce this spring, farmers are (     ) to conserve irrigation water.
items.explanation: この春は降水量が異例に少ないため、農家が農業用水を節約しようと「懸命に努力している」striving。
distractorReasons: fadeは「色あせる、消えゆく」。
trembleは「震える」。
strive to doで「〜しようと懸命に努める」。
boastは「自慢する」。
items.translation: この春は雨が異例に少ないため、農家はかんがい用水を節約しようと懸命に努めています。

items.prompt: The two eyewitnesses gave (     ) accounts of the accident, so police had to check nearby security cameras.
items.explanation: 防犯カメラを確認しなければならなくなったのは、2人の目撃者が「互いに矛盾する」証言をしたため。
distractorReasons: contradictory accountsで「食い違う・矛盾する証言」。
identicalは「全く同じ」で再確認の理由になりにくい。
obedientは「従順な」。
gratefulは「感謝している」。
items.translation: 2人の目撃者が事故について食い違う証言をしたため、警察は近くの防犯カメラを確認しなければなりませんでした。

items.prompt: Regular exercise can help (     ) the negative effects of sitting at a desk all day.
items.explanation: 一日中机に座っていることによる悪影響を定期的な運動が「打ち消す・相殺する」のでcounteract。
distractorReasons: exaggerateは「誇張する」。
cultivateは「耕す、育む」でnegative effectsを目的語にしない。
prosecuteは「起訴する」。
counteractは「悪影響などを打ち消す、中和する」。
items.translation: 定期的な運動は一日中デスクに座っていることによる悪影響を打ち消す助けになります。

items.prompt: The airline offered meal vouchers to passengers as (     ) for the five-hour flight delay.
items.explanation: 5時間の便遅延に対する「補償・おわび」として食事券を提供したのでcompensation。
distractorReasons: superstitionは「迷信」。
proportionは「割合・均衡」。
legislationは「法律・立法」。
compensation for ...で「〜に対する補償・埋め合わせ」。
items.translation: 航空会社は5時間のフライト遅延に対する補償として乗客に食事券を提供しました。

items.prompt: Although the new battery is slightly heavier, its capacity is (     ) superior to that of the previous model.
items.explanation: 少し重いものの容量は前モデルより「はるかに」優れているという譲歩からの強調なのでvastly。
distractorReasons: barelyは「かろうじて」で譲歩節Althoughとの対比が弱まる。
reluctantlyは「しぶしぶ」。
vastly superior to ...で「〜よりはるかに優れている」。
casuallyは「何気なく」。
items.translation: 新しいバッテリーはわずかに重くなっていますが、その容量は前のモデルよりはるかに優れています。

items.prompt: Dr. Patel's lecture was so technical that most first-year students could not (     ) her main point.
items.explanation: 専門的すぎたため多くの1年生が要点を「理解する・つかむ」ことができなかった、なのでgrasp。
distractorReasons: flatterは「お世辞を言う」。
grasp the main pointで「要点を把握する・理解する」。
postponeは「延期する」。
wanderは「歩き回る」。
items.translation: パテル博士の講義はあまりに専門的だったので、ほとんどの1年生は彼女の要点を理解できませんでした。

items.prompt: When assembling the steel shelf, please follow the numbered steps (     ) sequence.
items.explanation: in sequenceで「順番通りに」。番号のついた手順を順番通りに進める。
distractorReasons: on sequenceとは言わない。
by sequenceとは言わない。
at sequenceとは言わない。
in sequenceで「順序通りに、順を追って」。
items.translation: スチール棚を組み立てる際は、番号のついた手順に順番通りに従ってください。

items.prompt: The small publishing house managed to stay afloat (     ) a series of popular children's science books.
items.explanation: 人気の児童向け科学書シリーズ「のおかげで」経営を維持できたのでby virtue ofを選ぶ。

passage.title: Why Hospital Signs Stopped Using Medical Department Names
passage.text:
Large hospitals can be intimidating places to navigate, especially for anxious patients arriving for the first time. Traditionally, corridor signs directed visitors using formal medical terms such as "Otolaryngology," "Nephrology," or "Ophthalmology." To doctors and nurses, these names were precise and unambiguous. To many patients and family members, however, the unfamiliar Latin and Greek words slowed them down and forced them to stop staff in hallways for directions.

When a regional medical center renovated its main building, a communication researcher observed visitors at the entrance desk for two weeks. Nearly forty percent of inquiries came from people who already held appointment slips yet could not match the technical department name to everyday language. The hospital had inadvertently designed its signs for people who already worked there rather than for (18).

During the redesign, planners replaced complex terminology on main hallway signs with plain descriptions such as "Ear, Nose & Throat," "Kidney Care," and "Eye Clinic," accompanied by numbered color bands along the walls. Specialist terms were still printed in smaller letters underneath so medical referrals remained exact. (19), nurses spent far less time giving basic directions, and fewer patients arrived late for appointments.

The project demonstrated that accuracy and clarity need not conflict. Keeping technical terms on medical records while using everyday words on public signs allowed the hospital to (20).
passage.translation: 大病院は初めて訪れる不安な患者にとって迷いやすい場所だ。従来、院内の案内表示には「耳鼻咽喉科」「腎臓内科」「眼科」に相当する難解なラテン語・ギリシャ語由来の正式医学名称が使われてきた。医師や看護師には正確でも、多くの患者や家族にはなじみが薄く、廊下で職員を呼び止めて道を尋ねる原因になっていた。ある地域医療センターが本館を改修した際、研究者が受付を2週間観察したところ、質問の約4割は予約票を持っているのに専門診療科名と日常語が結びつかない人からのものだった。病院は無意識のうちに、(18)ではなく院内で働く人向けに標識を作っていたのだ。再設計では主廊下の表示を「耳・鼻・のど」「腎臓ケア」「目のクリニック」といった平易な表現と色分け番号帯に改め、紹介状との照合用に正式名称を小さく併記した。(19)、看護師が道案内に費やす時間は大幅に減り、予約に遅れる患者も減少した。診療記録の専門性と館内表示の分かりやすさを両立させたこの取り組みは、病院が(20)ことを可能にしたのである。

passage.title: Planting Pocket Forests in Industrial Districts
passage.text:
Urban tree-planting campaigns often place single young trees at regular intervals along concrete sidewalks. While tidy in appearance, isolated street trees frequently struggle in compacted soil, suffer from heat reflected off asphalt, and grow slowly. In paved industrial districts where summer temperatures rise sharply, planners have begun testing an alternative approach known as "pocket forests."

Instead of spacing one species evenly along a curb, landscapers loosen a plot of soil no larger than a tennis court, enrich it with compost, and plant dozens of native tree and shrub species close together. Because the young plants compete gently for sunlight while shading the soil beneath them, moisture evaporates more slowly and roots establish themselves rapidly. Within three years, a dense multi-layered canopy can form, creating (21).

Critics initially questioned whether tiny plots could make any measurable difference beside busy warehouses. Temperature sensors installed by university researchers showed that air directly inside and downwind of the pocket forests was several degrees cooler on summer afternoons than surrounding parking lots. (22), factory workers began using benches beside the plots during lunch breaks, and songbirds returned to areas where they had rarely been seen.

Planners emphasize that pocket forests are not a substitute for large suburban parks, which offer sports fields and long walking trails. Rather, their strength lies in (23) where large expanses of open land are simply unavailable.
passage.translation: 都市の植樹事業ではコンクリートの歩道沿いに単一種の若木を等間隔に植えることが多い。見た目は整っていても、孤立した街路樹は踏み固められた土壌やアスファルトの照り返しに苦しみ成長も遅い。夏の気温が急上昇する舗装だらけの工業地区では、「ポケット・フォレスト（小さな森）」と呼ばれる別手法の試験が始まっている。縁石沿いに1種ずつ離して植える代わりに、テニスコートほどの区画の土をほぐして堆肥を混ぜ、数十種の在来樹木や低木を密植する。若木同士が日光を求めて適度に競い合い足元の土に影を作るため、水分の蒸発が抑えられ根が素早く張る。3年以内に多層の樹冠が茂り、(21)を生み出す。当初は倉庫街の小さな区画に効果があるのか疑問視する声もあったが、大学研究者の温度計は夏の午後に区画内や風下の気温が周辺駐車場より数度低いことを示した。(22)、工場で働く人々が昼休みに横のベンチを使い始め、めったに見られなかった野鳥も戻ってきた。計画担当者は、運動場や長い遊歩道を備える郊外の大公園に取って代わるものではなく、広い土地が確保できない場所で(23)点にこそ強みがあると強調する。

passage.title: Notice Regarding the Archive Digitization Project
passage.text:
From: Marcus Vance, Head Archivist
To: Part-Time Scanning Assistants
Subject: Updated procedures for the newspaper collection

Dear assistants,
Thank you for your steady work digitizing our nineteenth-century town newspapers. Over the past month, our online archive has already been used by local high schools and historical researchers. As we move on to the older 1870–1885 volumes next Monday, we need to adjust two workflow rules to protect fragile paper.

First, please stop using the automatic sheet feeder completely. Even single pages from the 1870s are brittle along the margins and may tear if pulled by rollers. Every page must be placed by hand onto the overhead flatbed camera. This will reduce the number of pages scanned per hour, so we have removed the daily page target that applied last month. Quality and preservation take priority over speed.

Second, when an article contains faded ink that optical software cannot read reliably, please mark the file with the tag "MANUAL-CHECK" rather than guessing the missing words yourself. Our senior historians will review flagged pages every Thursday.

White cotton gloves turned out to reduce finger sensitivity and actually caused more accidental creases, so please wash and dry your hands thoroughly before each shift instead of wearing gloves. Let me know if you need training on the overhead camera before Monday.

Sincerely,
Marcus Vance
passage.translation: 差出人マーカス・ヴァンス（主任アーキビスト）、宛先スキャン補助スタッフ各位、件名：新聞コレクションの作業手順変更について。19世紀の町内新聞デジタル化への着実な取り組みに感謝。先月来すでに地元高校や歴史研究者に活用されている。来週月曜からさらに古い1870〜1885年分の冊子に入るため、もろい紙を保護する目的で手順を2点変更する。第1に、自動原稿送り装置の使用を全面中止すること。1870年代の紙は端がもろくローラーで破れる恐れがあるため、全ページを手作業で上向きフラットベッドカメラに置くこと。時間あたりの枚数は減るため、先月設けていた1日の枚数目標は撤廃した（速度より品質と保存を優先）。第2に、インクのかすれで文字認識ソフトが正確に読めない箇所は、自分で推測して補わず「MANUAL-CHECK」タグを付けること（毎週木曜に専門研究員が確認する）。また白い綿手袋は指先の感覚を鈍らせかえって折り目を作る原因になったため、手袋は着用せずシフト前に手洗いと乾燥を徹底すること。月曜前にカメラ研修が必要なら連絡してほしい。

貴重な資料を捨てる指示はない。

原本に直接ペンで書き込むのは厳禁。

items.prompt: Why does timetable punctuality matter greatly on quiet suburban bus routes?
choices: Buses run every five minutes throughout the day.
Delivery vans are banned from all suburban roads.
Passengers face a long wait if they miss a scheduled bus.
Suburban buses never stop for boarding passengers.
items.explanation: 1時間に2本程度の郊外路線では1本逃すと30分待つことになるため、時刻表通りの到着が重要になる。
distractorReasons: 5分間隔なのは都市部の幹線。
配送車全面禁止の記述はない。
Missing the 9:10 bus means waiting thirty minutesと一致。

passage.title: Rethinking How Cities Measure Bus Punctuality
passage.text:
Most city bus networks judge their performance by a familiar standard: whether each bus arrives at stops at the exact minute printed on the timetable. On quiet suburban routes that run twice an hour, this measure makes complete sense. Missing the 9:10 bus means waiting thirty minutes in the cold, so passengers check the clock before leaving home.

On busy urban corridors where buses are scheduled every five or six minutes, however, passengers behave differently. Commuters rarely consult a timetable; they simply walk to the stop expecting a bus to appear shortly. Yet heavy traffic frequently causes a frustrating pattern known as "bus bunching." If one bus is delayed for ninety seconds by a delivery van, slightly more passengers gather at the next stop. Boarding takes longer, delaying that bus further, while the following bus encounters almost empty stops and catches up. Soon two or three buses travel nose to tail, followed by a fifteen-minute gap.

Curiously, under traditional punctuality rules, an operator could try to keep drivers tied to fixed clock times even after traffic disrupted the pattern, or penalize drivers who paused briefly to restore spacing. When transit planners in Harborview analyzed passenger complaints, they realized riders on high-frequency routes did not care which specific bus they boarded; they cared about how long they waited on the sidewalk.

Harborview subsequently switched its evaluation of six-minute routes from timetable adherence to "headway regularity," which means keeping the time interval between consecutive buses steady. Dispatchers gained authority to ask an ahead-of-schedule bus to wait forty seconds at a transfer hub so a gap would not widen downstream. Digital signs at stops also began showing "Every 6 minutes" alongside live countdowns rather than long lists of clock times.

Average waiting times fell by nearly twenty percent without adding extra vehicles or drivers. Nevertheless, transit specialists note that headway management works only when routes are frequent and dispatchers communicate clearly with passengers on board; nobody likes sitting at a stop for forty seconds unless the driver explains why. Choosing the right metric, they conclude, depends on matching measurement to how passengers actually experience a journey.
passage.translation: 多くの都市バス網は「時刻表通りの分に各停留所へ到着したか」で運行成績を評価している。1時間に2本の静かな郊外路線ではこの指標は極めて合理的だ。9時10分の便を逃せば寒い中30分待つため、乗客は時計を見て家を出る。しかし5〜6分間隔で走る都市部の幹線では乗客の行動が異なる。乗客は時刻表を見ず、すぐ来るだろうと停留所へ向かう。ところが混雑した道路では「団子運転（バス・バンチング）」が頻発する。1台が配送車で90秒遅れると次の停留所で乗客が増え、乗車に時間がかかってさらに遅れる一方、後続便は空いた停留所を素早く通過して追いつき、2〜3台が続行した後に15分の空白が生じるのだ。奇妙なことに従来の定時性基準では間隔調整のための小休止が減点対象にさえなり得た。ハーバービュー市の交通計画担当者が苦情を分析すると、高頻度路線の乗客が気にしているのは「どの便に乗れたか」ではなく「歩道で何分待ったか」だった。そこで同市は6分間隔路線の評価基準を時刻表順守から「運行間隔の均等性」へ切り替え、先行しすぎた便に乗換拠点で40秒待機して後続との間隔を保つ指示を出せるようにした。車両や運転手を増やさずに平均待ち時間は約20％短縮された。もっとも専門家は、この手法が高頻度路線かつ車内放送での丁寧な理由説明とセットで初めて機能すると指摘し、乗客の実際の利用体験に合った指標選びの重要性を結論づけている。

items.prompt: How does "bus bunching" occur on busy urban routes?
choices: All drivers intentionally take lunch breaks at the same stop.
A small initial delay increases boarding time, allowing the next bus to catch up.
Passengers refuse to board the first bus that arrives.
Timetables schedule three buses to depart at the exact same minute.
items.explanation: 最初のわずかな遅れで次の停留所の待客と乗車時間が増えさらに遅れる一方、後続便は乗客が少なく追いついてしまう連鎖で起きる。
distractorReasons: 運転手が一斉に昼休みを取るからではない。
第2段落のメカニズム説明と完全に一致する。
乗客が最初のバスを拒否するのではない。
最初から同時刻に3台設定しているわけではない。
items.translation: 混雑する都市路線で「団子運転」はどのように発生しますか。

passage.title: Rethinking How Cities Measure Bus Punctuality
passage.text:
Most city bus networks judge their performance by a familiar standard: whether each bus arrives at stops at the exact minute printed on the timetable. On quiet suburban routes that run twice an hour, this measure makes complete sense. Missing the 9:10 bus means waiting thirty minutes in the cold, so passengers check the clock before leaving home.

On busy urban corridors where buses are scheduled every five or six minutes, however, passengers behave differently. Commuters rarely consult a timetable; they simply walk to the stop expecting a bus to appear shortly. Yet heavy traffic frequently causes a frustrating pattern known as "bus bunching." If one bus is delayed for ninety seconds by a delivery van, slightly more passengers gather at the next stop. Boarding takes longer, delaying that bus further, while the following bus encounters almost empty stops and catches up. Soon two or three buses travel nose to tail, followed by a fifteen-minute gap.

Curiously, under traditional punctuality rules, an operator could try to keep drivers tied to fixed clock times even after traffic disrupted the pattern, or penalize drivers who paused briefly to restore spacing. When transit planners in Harborview analyzed passenger complaints, they realized riders on high-frequency routes did not care which specific bus they boarded; they cared about how long they waited on the sidewalk.

Harborview subsequently switched its evaluation of six-minute routes from timetable adherence to "headway regularity," which means keeping the time interval between consecutive buses steady. Dispatchers gained authority to ask an ahead-of-schedule bus to wait forty seconds at a transfer hub so a gap would not widen downstream. Digital signs at stops also began showing "Every 6 minutes" alongside live countdowns rather than long lists of clock times.

Average waiting times fell by nearly twenty percent without adding extra vehicles or drivers. Nevertheless, transit specialists note that headway management works only when routes are frequent and dispatchers communicate clearly with passengers on board; nobody likes sitting at a stop for forty seconds unless the driver explains why. Choosing the right metric, they conclude, depends on matching measurement to how passengers actually experience a journey.

items.prompt: 以下の英文を読んで、その内容を英語で要約し、解答欄に記入しなさい。本文にない自分の意見は加えないこと。（目安語数：45〜55語）

passage.title: Returning Packaging Through Local Delivery Vans
passage.text:
As online shopping continues to grow, households receive millions of cardboard boxes and protective plastic cushions every week. Although cardboard can often be recycled through municipal collection, bulky packing materials quickly fill household bins, and manufacturing single-use boxes consumes considerable water and timber.

To address this issue, several delivery companies have begun testing reusable folding containers made of durable lightweight plastic. When a driver delivers a new order to an apartment building, customers can hand back flattened containers from previous deliveries so the van carries them back on its return trip.

However, the system faces practical challenges. Storing empty containers requires warehouse space, and some customers forget to return them promptly. To encourage timely returns, participating retailers now offer small shipping discounts whenever a container is scanned back at the door.
passage.translation:
ネット通販の拡大に伴い、各家庭には毎週膨大な段ボール箱や緩衝材が届いている。段ボールは自治体の回収でリサイクルできることが多いものの、かさばる梱包材は家庭のごみ箱をすぐに埋め、使い捨て箱の製造には大量の水や木材が消費される。
この問題に対処するため、複数の配送会社が丈夫で軽いプラスチック製の折りたたみ式通い箱の試験を始めた。配達員が集合住宅へ新しい荷物を届ける際、客が前回の箱をたたんで返却すれば帰りの便で回収できる。
しかし課題もある。空箱の保管には倉庫面積が要り、返却を忘れる客もいる。そこで参加小売店は、玄関先で箱の返却スキャンが完了するたびに少額の送料割引を提供して早期返却を促している。

items.model: Growing online shopping creates bulky packaging waste and consumes natural resources. Consequently, several delivery companies are testing reusable folding containers collected from customers during later deliveries. However, storing empty containers requires warehouse space and customers sometimes forget to return them, so participating retailers offer small shipping discounts to encourage prompt returns.
items.translation: 拡大するネット通販はかさばる梱包ごみを生み天然資源を消費する。そのため複数の配送会社は次回配達時に客から回収する再利用可能な折りたたみ容器を試している。しかし空箱の保管には倉庫面積が必要で客が返却を忘れることもあるため、参加小売店は少額の送料割引を行って迅速な返却を促している。
items.explanation: 第1段落の背景（通販拡大に伴う梱包ごみと資源消費）、第2段落の取り組み（次回配達時に回収する折りたたみ再利用容器）、第3段落の課題と対策（倉庫面積や返却忘れに対し送料割引で促進）を51語で過不足なく要約しています。
rubric: 通販の拡大に伴う梱包材廃棄・資源消費の背景を示した
折りたたみ式再利用容器の配達時回収の仕組みを含めた
保管場所・返却忘れの課題と送料割引による対策を結んだ
自分の意見を加えず45〜55語の目安に収めた

items.prompt:
次のTOPICについて、あなたの意見とその理由を2つ書きなさい。POINTSは理由を書く際の参考として自由に用いてかまいません。（目安語数：80〜100語）
TOPIC: Today, some museums allow visitors to take photographs of exhibits without flash. Do you think more museums should adopt this policy?
POINTS:
• Education
• Promotion
• Manners
items.model:
I think more museums should allow visitors to take photographs of exhibits without using flash.
First, photographs are valuable for education. Visitors often see hundreds of historical objects during a single visit and cannot remember every detail. Reviewing their own pictures at home helps students and researchers deepen their understanding.
Second, visitor photos serve as effective promotion. When people share favorite exhibits with friends or online, more young people become interested in visiting museums in person.
As long as quiet manners are enforced, flash-free photography benefits both visitors and museums.
items.translation:
私はより多くの博物館や美術館が、フラッシュを使わない展示物の写真撮影を来館者に認めるべきだと思います。
第一に、写真は教育面で有益です。来館者は1回の訪問で何百もの歴史的資料を目にするため細部まで覚えきれませんが、帰宅後に自分の写真を見返せば生徒や研究者は理解を深められます。
第二に、来館者の写真は効果的な広報になります。お気に入りの展示を友人やネット上で共有すれば、実際に足を運びたいと思う若者が増えます。
静かに鑑賞するマナーが守られる限り、フラッシュなしの撮影は来館者と施設の双方に利益をもたらします。
items.explanation: POINTSのEducationとPromotionを軸に、結論でMannersの条件も自然に添えて90語で論理的に構成しています。
rubric: 賛否の立場を冒頭で明確に示した
教育効果・広報効果など2つの異なる理由を具体的に展開した
語彙・構文を適切に使い段落構成を整えた
80〜100語の目安に収まっている

passage.title: Why Supermarkets Are Rethinking "Best-Before" Date Labels
passage.text:
Walk down any grocery aisle and you will see dozens of date stamps printed on milk cartons, canned beans, and bags of rice. Shoppers naturally assume these dates mark the exact day food becomes unsafe to eat. Food safety agencies point out, however, that two very different labels are often confused. While "use-by" dates apply to highly perishable items like raw fish, "best-before" dates on dry or canned goods indicate peak flavor and texture rather than spoilage.

Household surveys across several countries have revealed that nearly a third of still-edible groceries are thrown out simply because a "best-before" date has passed by a day or two. Consumers want to keep their families safe, yet inconsistent wording such as "sell by," "enjoy by," and "best if used before" leaves people guessing and encourages (18).

To clear up this confusion, several supermarket chains have standardized their packaging down to just two phrases: "Use By" for safety-critical chilled foods, and "Best Quality Before (Often Good Longer)" for shelf-stable items. Some dairy producers even add simple reminders instructing shoppers to look and smell before discarding unopened yogurt. (19), households participating in pilot studies threw away significantly less pantry food over six months.

Experts emphasize that clearer wording never lowers hygiene standards. Instead, distinguishing genuine safety deadlines from quality estimates helps consumers (20).
passage.translation: 食料品売り場を歩けば牛乳パックや豆の缶詰、米袋に多くの日付表示が印字されている。買い物客はそれが食べられなくなる境界日だと考えがちだが、食品安全機関は2種類の異なる表示が混同されていると指摘する。生魚などの傷みやすい食品に付く「消費期限（use-by）」に対し、乾物や缶詰の「賞味期限（best-before）」は腐敗ではなく風味や食感の目安を示している。各国の家庭調査では、まだ食べられる食料品の約3分の1が賞味期限を1〜2日過ぎただけの理由で捨てられていると判明した。家族の安全を守りたい消費者にとって、「販売期限」など不統一な表現が推測を生み、(18)を招いているのだ。この混乱を解消するため、複数のスーパーチェーンが安全に関わる要冷蔵品は「消費期限」、常温保存品は「おいしさの目安（以後も可）」の2表現に統一し、未開封ヨーグルトを捨てる前に見た目や匂いを確かめる案内を添える乳業メーカーも現れた。(19)、試験調査に参加した家庭では半年間の食品廃棄が大幅に減少した。明確な表示は衛生基準を下げるものではなく、安全上の期限と品質目安を区別することで消費者が(20)助けになる。

passage.title: Why Night Trains Are Making a Quiet Comeback in Europe
passage.text:
Twenty years ago, overnight sleeper trains across Europe seemed destined to disappear. Budget airlines offered cheap one-hour flights between major capitals, while daytime high-speed rail shortened medium-distance journeys. Maintaining sleeping carriages, which carry far fewer seats per car than ordinary trains, appeared unprofitable for national railways.

In recent years, however, traveler priorities have shifted noticeably. Airport security lines, luggage surcharges, and long bus rides from outlying airports often turn a short flight into a five-hour ordeal. Boarding an evening sleeper train in one city center and waking up next morning in another allows passengers to combine travel time with a night's hotel stay, turning hours that would otherwise be lost into (21).

Newer rolling stock has also addressed old complaints about noisy wheels and shared six-bunk compartments. Modern sleeper carriages feature quieter suspension, individual reading lamps, and compact single-berth capsules with sliding privacy doors for solo travelers. (22), routes linking Vienna, Zurich, Amsterdam, and Berlin now sell out weeks ahead during peak holiday months.

Transport economists acknowledge that overnight trains still face hurdles, such as coordinating track access fees across national borders. Even so, modern sleepers fill a valuable niche where distances are (23).
passage.translation: 20年前、ヨーロッパの夜行寝台列車は消えゆく運命にあると思われていた。格安航空会社が主要都市間を安価な1時間フライトで結び、昼間の高速鉄道が中距離移動を短縮するなか、1両あたりの定員が少ない寝台車の維持は採算が合わないと見られていたからだ。しかし近年、旅行者の優先事項は目に見えて変化した。空港の保安検査の列や手荷物追加料金、郊外空港からの長いバス移動により、短時間の飛行が5時間もの苦労になることも珍しくない。都心の駅から夜の寝台列車に乗り翌朝別の都心で目覚めれば、移動時間とホテル1泊を兼ねることができ、本来失われるはずの時間を(21)に変えられる。新型車両は車輪の騒音や6人相部屋といった従来の不満も解消し、静かなサスペンションや個別読書灯、一人旅向けの鍵付き個室カプセルを備えている。(22)、ウィーン・チューリッヒ・アムステルダム・ベルリンを結ぶ路線は繁忙期には数週間前に完売するほどだ。国境をまたぐ線路使用料の調整など課題は残るものの、現代の寝台列車は距離が(23)区間で貴重な役割を果たしている。

passage.title: Update on the Botanical Conservatory Roof Renewal
passage.text:
From: Elena Rostova, Director of Visitor Operations
To: Annual Pass Holders
Subject: Temporary Palm Dome closure and membership extension

Dear Annual Pass Holders,
Thank you for your continued support of the Midvale Botanical Conservatory. Beginning Monday, September 14, our central Palm Dome will close for ten weeks so engineers can replace its forty-year-old single-pane glass panels with insulated UV-balanced glazing. The new roof will cut winter heating fuel use by thirty-five percent while protecting tropical ferns from summer leaf burn.

During the construction period, the Desert House, Alpine Rock Garden, and Orchid Pavilion will remain open during regular hours. In addition, our horticulture curators will offer free thirty-minute behind-the-scenes tours of the propagation greenhouses every Wednesday and Saturday at 11:00 a.m. exclusively for Annual Pass Holders (up to fifteen guests per tour; sign up at the reception desk on the day of your visit).

Because the Palm Dome is our largest indoor attraction, every active Annual Pass as of September 14 will automatically be extended by two full months at no cost. You do not need to replace your plastic card; our gate scanner will update your expiration date automatically.

Please note that the east parking lot will be used by crane trucks until mid-November, so drivers should enter through the West Willow Gate instead.

Warm regards,
Elena Rostova

items.prompt: How can Annual Pass Holders join the propagation greenhouse tour?

items.translation: 年間パスポート会員はどのように育苗温室ツアーに参加できますか。

items.prompt: How did twentieth-century hospital planners traditionally regard outdoor gardens?
choices: As the most important treatment room in every hospital.
As dangerous places that caused surgical infections.
As areas reserved exclusively for ambulance helicopters.
As optional decorations secondary to clinical efficiency.
items.explanation: 20世紀の病院建築は効率を最優先し、木々や庭は予算が余った場合にのみ残す装飾品（pleasant decorations）として扱っていた。

感染症の原因とされた記述はない。
ヘリポート専用という記述はない。
prioritized clinical efficiency ... treated trees and gardens as pleasant decorations that were worth keeping only if money was left overと一致。
items.translation: 20世紀の病院設計者は従来、屋外の庭園をどのように捉えていましたか。

passage.title: How Hospital Courtyards Speed Up Patient Recovery
passage.text:
For much of the twentieth century, modern hospital architecture prioritized clinical efficiency above almost everything else. Long windowless corridors minimized walking distances between operating rooms and laboratories, while outdoor courtyards were often paved over to expand equipment wings or staff parking. Architects treated trees and gardens as pleasant decorations that were worth keeping only if money was left over.

That view began to change after health researchers compared surgical patients whose rooms overlooked a small grove of maple trees with similar patients facing a plain brick wall. Reviewing hospital charts over several years, researchers noticed a consistent pattern: patients with a view of greenery requested fewer strong painkillers, reported lower anxiety, and were discharged nearly a day earlier on average than those facing brick.

Subsequent studies examined what happened when patients, visiting relatives, and nurses could actually step outside into a sheltered courtyard for fifteen minutes. Measuring heart rates and stress hormones showed that sitting near running water and varied foliage helped the nervous system recover from the constant beeping of medical monitors. Equally important, nurses who took breaks in green courtyards made fewer clerical errors during afternoon shifts than colleagues who rested in windowless basement lounges.

Designing an effective healing garden involves more than scattering flowerpots on concrete. Landscape specialists work closely with physical therapists to build wide, non-slip pathways gentle enough for wheelchairs and IV poles, provide shaded seating every ten meters so recovering patients can rest easily, and avoid heavily scented flowers that might discomfort people experiencing nausea.

Today, hospital administrators increasingly view therapeutic gardens not as luxury ornaments, but as practical medical infrastructure that supports patients, families, and exhausted clinical staff alike.
passage.translation: 20世紀の多くの期間、近代病院建築は何よりも臨床効率を優先してきた。手術室と検査室の移動距離を縮める窓のない長い廊下が作られ、中庭は医療機器棟や職員駐車場の拡張のために舗装されることが多く、樹木や庭園は予算が余ったときだけの装飾と見なされていた。この見方が変わり始めたきっかけは、カエデの小さな木立が見える病室の術後患者と、無地のレンガ壁に面した同様の患者を比較した研究だった。数年分のカルテを分析すると、緑が見える患者は強い鎮痛剤の要請が少なく、不安も低く、平均して約1日早く退院していた。さらに患者や家族、看護師が実際に中庭へ15分間出られる場合を調べた後続研究では、水音や多様な植物のそばに座ることで医療モニターの電子音にさらされた神経系の回復が促されると心拍数やストレスホルモン値から確認された。同様に重要な点として、緑の中庭で休憩した看護師は窓のない地下休憩室で休んだ同僚よりも午後の勤務での事務ミスが少なかった。効果的な「癒やしの庭」の設計は鉢植えを並べるだけではない。造園家は理学療法士と連携し、車椅子や点滴スタンドでも通りやすい幅広で滑りにくい歩道を整備し、10メートルごとに日陰のベンチを置き、吐き気のある患者の負担になる強い香りの花を避ける。今日、病院経営者は治療庭園を贅沢な飾りではなく、患者・家族・医療スタッフ全員を支える実用的な医療インフラと捉えるようになっている。

items.prompt: What did the comparison between patients seeing maple trees and those facing a brick wall reveal?
choices: Both groups stayed in the hospital for the exact same number of days.
Patients facing the brick wall recovered faster because rooms were darker.
Maple pollen forced the hospital to seal every bedroom window.
Patients overlooking trees needed less strong pain medicine and went home sooner.
items.explanation: カエデの木立が見える病室の患者は、レンガ壁向きの患者に比べて強い鎮痛剤の要請が少なく、平均で約1日早く退院していた。
distractorReasons: 入院日数は木立側のほうが約1日短かった。
レンガ壁側のほうが早く回復したのではない。
花粉で窓を封鎖した記述はない。
requested fewer strong painkillers ... and were discharged nearly a day earlierと一致。
items.translation: カエデの木立が見える患者とレンガ壁に面した患者の比較から何が明らかになりましたか。

Medical monitors were moved permanently into the outdoor garden.
items.explanation: 緑のある中庭で休憩をとった看護師は、窓のない地下ラウンジで休んだ同僚に比べて午後シフトでの事務的ミスが少なかった。

items.translation: 緑のある中庭は病院で働く看護師たちにどのような影響を与えましたか。

Landscape specialists work closely with physical therapists to build wide, non-slip pathways gentle enough for wheelchairs and IV poles, provide shaded seating every ten meters so recovering patients can rest easily, and avoid heavily scented flowers that might discomfort people experiencing nausea.

Today, hospital administrators increasingly view therapeutic gardens not as luxury ornaments, but as practical medical infrastructure that supports patients, families, and exhausted clinical staff alike.

passage.title: How Hospital Courtyards Speed Up Patient Recovery
passage.text:
For much of the twentieth century, modern hospital architecture prioritized clinical efficiency above almost everything else. Long windowless corridors minimized walking distances between operating rooms and laboratories, while outdoor courtyards were often paved over to expand equipment wings or staff parking. Architects treated trees and gardens as pleasant decorations that were worth keeping only if money was left over.

That view began to change after health researchers compared surgical patients whose rooms overlooked a small grove of maple trees with similar patients facing a plain brick wall. Reviewing hospital charts over several years, researchers noticed a consistent pattern: patients with a view of greenery requested fewer strong painkillers, reported lower anxiety, and were discharged nearly a day earlier on average than those facing brick.

Subsequent studies examined what happened when patients, visiting relatives, and nurses could actually step outside into a sheltered courtyard for fifteen minutes. Measuring heart rates and stress hormones showed that sitting near running water and varied foliage helped the nervous system recover from the constant beeping of medical monitors. Equally important, nurses who took breaks in green courtyards made fewer clerical errors during afternoon shifts than colleagues who rested in windowless basement lounges.

Designing an effective healing garden involves more than scattering flowerpots on concrete. Landscape specialists work closely with physical therapists to build wide, non-slip pathways gentle enough for wheelchairs and IV poles, provide shaded seating every ten meters so recovering patients can rest easily, and avoid heavily scented flowers that might discomfort people experiencing nausea.

Today, hospital administrators increasingly view therapeutic gardens not as luxury ornaments, but as practical medical infrastructure that supports patients, families, and exhausted clinical staff alike.

passage.title: Digital Textbooks in Secondary Schools
passage.text:
In recent years, many secondary schools have introduced tablet-based digital textbooks alongside or in place of printed volumes. Carrying a single lightweight tablet relieves students from heavy backpacks packed with thick books, while built-in audio players and adjustable font sizes help learners check pronunciation and read comfortably.

At the same time, teachers and students have noted drawbacks during daily lessons. Looking at backlit screens for several hours can cause eye strain, and incoming notifications or switching between pages makes it harder for some students to compare two chapters side by side or stay focused.

Consequently, a growing number of schools are adopting a hybrid approach, using tablets for listening exercises and multimedia maps while keeping printed workbooks for extended reading and handwritten notes.
passage.translation:
近年、多くの中学・高校で紙の教科書と併用、あるいはその代替としてタブレット型のデジタル教科書が導入されている。軽いタブレット1台にまとめることで分厚い本が詰まった重い通学かばんの負担が減り、内蔵音声や文字サイズ調整機能は発音確認や読みやすさに役立つ。
一方で日々の授業では欠点も指摘されている。長時間画面を見続けると目の疲れを招きやすく、通知やページ切り替えによって2つの章を見比べたり集中を保ったりしにくい生徒もいる。
そのため現在では、リスニング練習やマルチメディア地図にはタブレットを使い、長文読解や手書きノートには紙の教材を残す併用方式を採る学校が増えている。

items.explanation: 第1段落の利点（通学負担軽減・音声や文字調整機能）、第2段落の課題（眼精疲労・ページ比較や集中維持の難しさ）、第3段落の対応策（用途に応じたタブレットと紙教材のハイブリッド活用）を51語で正確に要約しています。

TOPIC: More cities are creating bicycle-only lanes along major roads. Do you think the number of such lanes should continue to increase?

• Environment
• Traffic congestion
items.model:
I strongly believe that the number of bicycle-only lanes along major roads should continue to increase.
First, separated lanes greatly improve safety for everyone. When cyclists do not have to weave between cars and pedestrians on narrow sidewalks, serious traffic accidents decrease significantly.
Second, expanding bike lanes benefits the environment. Safe routes encourage commuters and students to ride bicycles instead of driving cars for short trips, reducing exhaust emissions and noise.
For safer streets and cleaner urban air, cities should continue investing in dedicated bicycle lanes.
items.translation:
私は幹線道路沿いの自転車専用レーンの数を今後も増やし続けるべきだと強く思います。

第二に、自転車レーンの拡充は環境にも貢献します。安全な経路があれば通勤客や学生が短距離移動で車の代わりに自転車を使うようになり、排気ガスや騒音が減ります。
より安全な道路と澄んだ都市の空気のために、自治体は専用レーンへの投資を続けるべきです。

passage.title: Why Airport Carpets Quietly Calm Travelers
passage.text:
Major rail terminals tend to favor polished stone floors that withstand millions of rolling suitcases, yet many international airports still cover long departure piers with miles of patterned carpet. Cleaning carpet takes extra effort, so travelers sometimes wonder why operators keep installing soft flooring beyond security checkpoints.

Acoustics and pacing explain the choice. Hard stone corridors bounce announcements, footsteps, and wheel clatter back and forth, raising stress among passengers already worried about boarding times. Carpet absorbs high-frequency noise so gate calls remain intelligible at lower volume. Softer underfoot resistance also slows walking speed slightly without people realizing it. (18), crowds move more smoothly and waiting areas feel calmer.

Maintenance teams manage wear by laying modular carpet squares rather than single giant rolls. When coffee spills near a café or wheel tracks wear down a central lane, crews swap out only the damaged fifty-centimeter tiles overnight. passage.title: When Seaweed Farms Help Shellfish Neighbours
passage.text:
Along rocky coasts from Hokkaido to Maine, shellfish growers raising oysters and scallops face a quiet chemical challenge. As oceans absorb excess carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, coastal waters become slightly more acidic, making it harder for young shellfish larvae to build sturdy calcium shells during their first weeks of life.

Marine researchers testing ways to buffer local waters noticed a promising partner already familiar to coastal cuisine: fast-growing kelp and other seaweeds. Like land plants, kelp draws dissolved carbon dioxide out of seawater during daylight hours as it photosynthesizes. Hanging curtains of kelp on ropes just upstream of oyster cages measurably raises water pH in the surrounding bay while releasing oxygen. (21), juvenile oysters raised beside seaweed lines develop thicker shells than those grown in open water nearby.

Sharing ocean leases benefits farmers economically as well. Kelp grows fastest in cold winter and early spring months when shellfish work is relatively quiet, allowing crews to use the same boats, buoys, and anchor lines across seasons. Harvested seaweed can be sold for food, fertilizer, or animal feed supplements. (22), kelp blades absorb excess nitrogen washing off farmland, reducing summer algae blooms that otherwise suffocate coastal beds.

Co-cultivating seaweed and shellfish will not reverse global ocean chemistry on its own. Even so, pairing complementary marine crops gives coastal communities (23).
passage.translation: 北海道からメイン州に至る岩場の沿岸でカキやホタテを育てる養殖業者は、静かな化学的課題に直面しています。海が大気中の過剰な二酸化炭素を吸収するにつれ沿岸水がわずかに酸性化し、幼生が最初の数週間に丈夫なカルシウムの殻を作りにくくなっているのです。身近な海藻であるコンブ類に注目した海洋研究者は、日中の光合成でコンブが海水中の溶存二酸化炭素を吸収する働きを活かしました。カキかごの潮上にコンブのロープを吊るすと周囲のpHが目に見えて改善し酸素も放出されます。(21)、海藻ロープの隣で育った稚貝は近くの開けた海面より厚い殻を形成します。漁場の共用には経済的利点もあり、コンブは貝類の作業が比較的落ち着く厳冬から早春に最も成長するため、同じ船やブイ、錨綱を通年で活用でき、収穫物は食用や肥料・飼料になります。(22)、コンブの葉は農地から流れ込む過剰な窒素を吸収し、夏の赤潮や藻類の異常繁殖を抑えます。海藻と貝類の複合養殖だけで地球規模の海洋化学は変えられなくとも、相補的な海の作物の組み合わせは沿岸地域に(23)をもたらしています。

passage.title: Updated Procedures for Ceramic Kiln Firing
passage.text:
From: S. Takemoto, Community Craft Center
To: Advanced Pottery Members
Subject: Moisture checks and shelf tags before Friday's glaze firing

Dear pottery members,
Our monthly high-temperature glaze firing is scheduled for this Friday evening. During last month's run, one thick-walled flower vase cracked violently because moisture was still trapped deep inside the clay, scattering fragments onto neighboring bowls on the middle shelf. To protect everyone's work, we are introducing two mandatory steps starting this week.

First, all bisque-fired pieces glazed on Wednesday or Thursday must sit on the heated drying rack in Studio B for at least twenty-four hours before entering the kiln. Pieces glazed on Friday afternoon will be held over for next month's firing, with no exceptions.

Second, if you apply a runny ash glaze that tends to flow near 1,250 degrees Celsius, you must place your piece on a personal ceramic "cookie" slab and attach a yellow shelf tag. Staff load tagged items on the bottom shelf so any melted glaze drips onto your own slab rather than fusing permanently to the center's expensive silicon-carbide kiln shelves.

Unloading will begin Monday at 2:00 p.m., once the chamber has cooled below 60 degrees.

Best regards,
S. Takemoto
passage.translation: 地域工芸センターの竹本から上級陶芸会員への連絡。今月の高温本焼きは今週金曜夜に予定されている。先月の窯焚きでは、粘土の奥に水分が残っていた厚手の花瓶が激しく割れ、中段の周囲の器に破片が飛び散る事故があったため、今週から全員の作品を守る2つの必須ルールを導入する。第1に、水曜または木曜に施釉した素焼き作品は窯入れ前にB工房の温風乾燥棚で最低24時間乾燥させること（金曜午後に施釉した作品は例外なく来月回しとなる）。第2に、1250度付近で流れやすい灰釉を使う場合は必ず個人用の受け皿（トチ・クッキー板）の上に載せて黄色い棚札を付けること。センターの高価な炭化ケイ素製の棚板に溶けた釉薬が融着するのを防ぐため、札付きの作品はスタッフが最下段に詰める。窯出しは炉内が60度以下に冷めた月曜午後2時から行う。

Dear pottery members,
Our monthly high-temperature glaze firing is scheduled for this Friday evening. During last month's run, one thick-walled flower vase cracked violently because moisture was still trapped deep inside the clay, scattering fragments onto neighboring bowls on the middle shelf. To protect everyone's work, we are introducing two mandatory steps starting this week.

First, all bisque-fired pieces glazed on Wednesday or Thursday must sit on the heated drying rack in Studio B for at least twenty-four hours before entering the kiln. Pieces glazed on Friday afternoon will be held over for next month's firing, with no exceptions.

Second, if you apply a runny ash glaze that tends to flow near 1,250 degrees Celsius, you must place your piece on a personal ceramic "cookie" slab and attach a yellow shelf tag. Staff load tagged items on the bottom shelf so any melted glaze drips onto your own slab rather than fusing permanently to the center's expensive silicon-carbide kiln shelves.

Unloading will begin Monday at 2:00 p.m., once the chamber has cooled below 60 degrees.

Best regards,
S. Takemoto
passage.translation: 地域工芸センターの竹本から上級陶芸会員への連絡。今月の高温本焼きは今週金曜夜に予定されている。先月の窯焚きでは、粘土の奥に水分が残っていた厚手の花瓶が激しく割れ、中段の周囲の器に破片が飛び散る事故があったため、今週から全員の作品を守る2つの必須ルールを導入する。第1に、水曜または木曜に施釉した素焼き作品は窯入れ前にB工房の温風乾燥棚で最低24時間乾燥させること（金曜午後に施釉した作品は例外なく来月回しとなる）。第2に、1250度付近で流れやすい灰釉を使う場合は必ず個人用の受け皿（トチ・クッキー板）の上に載せて黄色い棚札を付けること。センターの高価な炭化ケイ素製の棚板に溶けた釉薬が融着するのを防ぐため、札付きの作品はスタッフが最下段に詰める。窯出しは炉内が60度以下に冷めた月曜午後2時から行う。

紙が溶けてプラスチックになるのではない。

passage.title: Why Packaging Engineers Study Origami Creases
passage.text:
Cardboard shipping boxes and beverage cartons look simple until you try designing one that folds flat in a warehouse, pops into shape on a high-speed filling line, resists crushing when stacked two meters high, and opens cleanly without scissors. Over the past fifteen years, packaging engineers seeking lighter, recyclable containers have found unexpected inspiration in the geometry of traditional Japanese origami.

In structural engineering, a flat sheet of thin paper bends effortlessly, yet adding a pattern of angled creases gives that same sheet remarkable stiffness. Aerospace researchers famously used "Miura-ori" folds to pack solar panels tightly inside rockets and unfold them in a single smooth pull in orbit. Packaging laboratories realized that similar crease networks could let thinner paperboard support heavy groceries or fragile electronics without relying on molded plastic foam inserts.

Origami geometry also cuts waste on factory floors. Conventional cushioned boxes often glue together three or four separate layers of cardboard and plastic film, making recycling awkward for households. A single die-cut sheet scored with precise valley and mountain folds, by contrast, can fold inward to form its own springy corner bumpers. Because no glue joins dissimilar materials, the entire package goes straight into standard paper recycling bins once unpacked.

Translating hand-folded art into industrial machinery has not been effortless. Paper fibers crack if bent too sharply at three hundred cartons per minute, and humid summer warehouses soften creases differently than dry winter air. Engineers therefore test fiber grain direction and press rounded micro-scores rather than sharp knife lines so folds flex reliably across seasons.

What began as centuries-old paper craft now helps manufacturers ship everyday goods with less bulk, less plastic, and smarter structural strength.
passage.translation: 段ボール箱や飲料パックは一見単純に見えますが、倉庫では平らに畳め、高速充填ラインで瞬時に立ち上がり、2メートルの高さに積んでも潰れず、はさみなしで綺麗に開く容器を設計するのは容易ではありません。過去15年、軽量でリサイクルしやすい容器を模索する包装技術者は、日本の伝統的な折り紙の幾何学から思いがけない着想を得てきました。薄い1枚の紙は簡単に曲がりますが、角度を計算した折り目パターンを加えると驚くほどの剛性が生まれます。宇宙工学で太陽電池パネルの収納・展開に使われた「三浦折り」などの原理を応用すれば、成形発泡プラスチックの緩衝材に頼らず薄い板紙だけで重い食品や精密機器を支えられます。また従来の緩衝箱は紙とプラスチックフィルムなど複数素材を接着するため家庭での分別が厄介でしたが、山折り・谷折りを精密に刻んだ1枚の抜き型シートなら内側に折り返すだけで弾力のある角当てになり、異素材の接着がないため使用後はそのまま古紙回収へ出せます。毎分300箱の高速機械で紙繊維が割れたり季節の湿度で折り癖が変わったりする課題も、繊維の目の向きや丸みのある微細な押し罫の工夫で克服されつつあります。

items.prompt: Why is a single folded paperboard insert easier for households to recycle than conventional cushioned boxes?
choices: Households must mail conventional boxes back to aerospace labs.
Standard recycling bins accept only plastic foam.
It forms springy corner bumpers from one material without gluing paper to plastic film.
Single-sheet boxes dissolve completely in kitchen sinks.
items.explanation: 従来品は複数の板紙とプラスチックフィルムを接着していたが、1枚のシートを折り込む方式なら異素材の接着がなくそのまま古紙回収に出せる。
distractorReasons: 宇宙研究所へ返送するのではない。
発泡スチロール専用ではない。
第3段落の記述と一致。
流し台で溶けるのではない。
items.translation: 従来の緩衝箱に比べ、1枚折りの板紙緩衝材が家庭でリサイクルしやすいのはなぜですか。

items.prompt: What manufacturing challenge did engineers face when adapting intricate folds to high-speed machines?
choices: Factory machines could fold only three cartons per day.
Beverage cartons were too large to fit inside warehouses.
Origami artists refused to share ruler measurements.
Paper fibers could crack at high speeds and seasonal humidity altered how creases behaved.
items.explanation: 毎分300箱の高速折り加工では急な角度で紙の繊維が割れやすく、夏の湿気と冬の乾燥で折り目の硬さが変わる課題があった。
distractorReasons: 1日3箱ではない。
倉庫に入らない大きさではない。
作家の拒否ではない。
第4段落の2つの技術課題と一致。
items.translation: 複雑な折りを高速機械へ応用する際、技術者はどんな製造上の課題に直面しましたか。

By folding every shipping box by hand at home.

items.explanation: 紙繊維の目（流れ）の向きを検証し、鋭い刃線ではなく丸みを持たせた微細な押し罫を入れることで季節を問わずしなやかに曲がるようにした。
distractorReasons: 油に浸すのではない。
家庭での手折りではない。
第4段落末の解決策と一致。
アルミ板への変更ではない。
items.translation: 高速生産ラインで紙の繊維が割れるのを防ぐため、技術者はどう工夫しましたか。

items.prompt: Which statement best summarizes the passage?
choices: Plastic foam remains the only safe material for shipping fragile electronics.
Traditional folding principles, refined through modern engineering, enable stronger and less wasteful packaging.
Origami techniques work well in space exploration but fail in everyday commerce.
Consumers prefer packages that require scissors and strong glue to open.
items.explanation: 長い歴史を持つ折り紙の構造原理が現代の製造技術で磨かれ、強くてプラスチックごみの少ない包装を実現している。
distractorReasons: 発泡材が唯一とは逆。
本文全体と最終文の要旨を的確に要約。
日用品輸送にも実用化されている。
はさみ不要で開けやすい設計が求められている。
items.translation: 本文全体を最もよく要約している文はどれですか。

items.prompt: The city water bureau urged households to (     ) leaking faucets promptly, as steady drips waste thousands of liters a year.
items.explanation: 水漏れする蛇口の問題を速やかに「直す・是正する」よう呼びかけたrectify。
distractorReasons: rectifyは不具合や誤りを直す・改める。
reciteは暗唱する。
revolveは回転する。
recedeは後退する。
items.translation: ポタポタ落ちる水滴だけでも年間何千リットルもの無駄になるため、市水道局は水漏れする蛇口を速やかに直すよう各家庭に促しました。

items.prompt: Because the island ferry carries fuel trucks only twice a week, gas stations must keep an (     ) reserve on hand.
items.explanation: 週2便しか燃料車を運ばないため、ガソリンスタンドは「十分な」備蓄を手元に保つ必要があるadequate。
distractorReasons: aridは乾燥した。
awkwardは気まずい・扱いにくい。
adequateは十分な・適切な量の。
abruptは突然の。
items.translation: 島のフェリーは週2回しか燃料トラックを運ばないため、ガソリンスタンドは十分な備蓄を手元に確保しておかなければなりません。

items.prompt: The journalist double-checked three independent archives so that no factual error would (     ) the credibility of her book.
items.explanation: 事実誤認が著書の信頼性を「損なう・弱める」ことがないよう3つの独立資料を照合したundermine。
distractorReasons: undertakeは引き受ける。
undermine credibilityで信頼性を損なう。
undergoは経験する・受ける。
underlineは強調する・下線を引く。
items.translation: 事実誤認によって著書の信頼性が損なわれることがないよう、そのジャーナリストは3つの独立した資料館で裏づけを取りました。

items.prompt: Entry to the astronomical observatory roof is granted strictly (     ) weather conditions on the mountain remain calm.
items.explanation: 山の気象条件が穏やかである「という条件でのみ（〜である場合に限り）」屋上への立ち入りが認められるprovided that＋節。
distractorReasons: apart fromも前置詞句。
in spite ofは前置詞句で節をとらない。
by virtue ofも前置詞句。
provided that＋節で「〜という条件で」。後ろに節が続く。
items.translation: 山の気象状況が穏やかである場合に限り、天文台の屋上への立ち入りが認められます。

items.prompt: When an unexpected frost hit the valley in April, orchard growers burned smudge pots to keep apple blossoms from (     ).
items.explanation: 4月の不意の霜に際し、リンゴの花が「しおれる・枯れる」のを防いだkeep ... from withering。
distractorReasons: witherは植物や花がしおれる・枯れる。
wanderは歩き回る。

passage.title: Why Supermarkets Put Doors on Open Chillers
passage.text:
Walk down the dairy aisle of an older supermarket, and cool air spills out from open refrigerated shelves. Store designers long favored open cases because shoppers could grab milk or yogurt in two seconds without touching a handle, boosting impulse purchases. Yet an open chiller leaks cold air continuously, forcing compressors in the back room to run almost nonstop.

Rising electricity bills prompted several grocery chains to test retrofitting existing cases with lightweight double-glazed glass doors. Managers worried that adding a physical barrier might hurt sales. When stores installed anti-fog glass and warm vertical LED strips inside the frames, however, sales remained steady while refrigeration electricity use plunged by up to forty percent. (18), aisles became noticeably more comfortable for shoppers who previously hurried past chilly zones.

Enclosed cases improved food quality as well. Open shelves suffer temperature swings near the front edge, whereas closed doors keep yogurt and cut fruit at a uniform three degrees Celsius. (19), spoilage dropped and staff spent less time rotating stock.

What once seemed a risky design change showed that (20).
passage.translation: 古いタイプのスーパーの乳製品売り場を歩くと、扉のないオープン冷蔵棚から冷気が通路へ流れ出しています。客が取っ手に触れず2秒で牛乳やヨーグルトを手に取れるため衝動買いが増えるとして長年好まれましたが、冷気が絶えず逃げるため裏の圧縮機はほぼ休みなく稼働し続けます。電気代の高騰を受け、複数のスーパーチェーンが既存の棚に軽量な複層ガラス扉を後付けする試験を行いました。当初は物理的な仕切りで売上が落ちる懸念もありましたが、曇り止めガラスと枠内の明るい縦型LED照明を組み合わせると、売上は維持されたまま冷蔵電力が最大4割も削減されました。(18)、以前は寒くて足早に通り過ぎていた買い物客にとっても通路が格段に快適になりました。密閉化は食品の品質も高め、前端の温度むらが出やすい開放棚と違って庫内を均一な3度に保てるため、(19)、廃棄が減り品出し入れ替えの手間も軽くなりました。かつて冒険と思われた設計変更は、(20)ことを示しました。

passage.title: When Soil Microbes Leave Clues for Archaeologists
passage.text:
Archaeologists searching for ancient timber buildings often face a frustrating reality: in damp, mild climates, wooden posts rot away completely within centuries, leaving neither stone walls nor brick foundations behind. Traditionally, excavators locate vanished halls by scraping away topsoil and looking for faint dark circles—known as postholes—where decayed wood stained the earth.

Visual stains, however, can be hard to distinguish from animal burrows or tree roots. Recently, geoarchaeologists have begun analyzing the DNA and chemical traces of soil bacteria living in buried layers. Centuries of human or livestock activity alter soil phosphorus, acidity, and organic matter in lasting ways. Even two thousand years after a wooden stable disappeared, the microbial community thriving in that patch of dirt differs measurably from the microbes three meters outside the wall. (21), researchers can tell whether a vanished room once housed cattle, stored grain, or served as a clean sleeping area.

Sampling tiny cores of soil with a hand auger also protects fragile sites. Rather than digging wide trenches across an entire meadow, teams test small pinprick samples first to map where activity was concentrated. (22), full excavation can be limited to the corners most likely to answer historical questions.

Microbial mapping does not replace trowels and pottery analysis, of course. Still, reading living microscopic ecosystems allows archaeologists to (23) long after timber walls have turned back to dust.

passage.title: Instructions for the Winter Roof-Snow Safety Inspection
passage.text:
From: Facilities Management Office
To: Second-Floor Laboratory Staff
Subject: Thursday morning roof clearing and window locks

Dear laboratory staff,
Following Tuesday's heavy snowfall, forty-five centimeters of wet snow has accumulated on the sloped roof of the North Research Wing. Because daytime temperatures are forecast to rise above six degrees on Friday, compacted snow could slide off suddenly and block emergency exits. A licensed snow-removal crew will therefore clear the roof this Thursday between 8:30 a.m. and 11:30 a.m.

For safety during those three hours, the walkway along the north wall will be cordoned off; please enter and exit the building solely through the south courtyard doors. In addition, ensure that all second-floor tilt windows are latched tightly before leaving work Wednesday evening, as snow pushed off the eaves can strike loose windowpanes.

Vibration from roof shovels may briefly disturb delicate balances on the second floor. If your team plans precision weighing under one milligram on Thursday morning, please reschedule it for the afternoon or use Balance Room 102 in the basement.

Regards,
Facilities Management Office

passage.title: How Seed Vaults Guard Crop Diversity Against New Risks
passage.text:
Modern supermarkets create an illusion of boundless agricultural variety, displaying dozens of breads, pastas, and snacks down long aisles. Genetically, however, global food supplies rely on a surprisingly narrow base. Over the past century, farmers understandably favored high-yielding wheat, rice, and maize varieties that ripened uniformly for mechanical harvesters, while thousands of local "landrace" varieties adapted to specific valleys or dry hillsides fell out of everyday cultivation.

Uniformity carries biological vulnerability. When vast regions plant genetically similar crops, a single newly evolved fungus, insect pest, or prolonged drought can sweep across entire harvests. Wild relatives and half-forgotten regional varieties often hold the exact genetic traits plant breeders need—such as tolerance to salty soil or resistance to a rust disease—even if their yields look modest on prime farmland.

To keep those traits from vanishing forever, more than 1,700 national and regional gene banks dry seeds to low moisture levels and store them in subzero chambers. High in the Arctic archipelago of Svalbard, a global backup vault carved deep inside frozen rock holds duplicate packets sent from collections worldwide, ensuring that regional power failures, floods, or civil conflicts do not erase irreplaceable agricultural heritage.

Yet frozen vaults alone are only half the solution. Seeds stored in jars eventually lose germination vigor after decades and must be planted out periodically to produce fresh stock. Moreover, a seed frozen in 1980 stops evolving alongside shifting climates and pests in real fields. Consequently, conservationists increasingly pair cold vaults with "living" on-farm networks, paying smallholder farmers to keep growing traditional varieties in their home landscapes.

Safeguarding tomorrow's harvests requires both the quiet insurance of subzero rock chambers and the ongoing adaptation of working fields.
passage.translation: 現代のスーパーの長い通路には無数のパンやパスタが並び豊かな多様性があるように見えますが、遺伝的に見ると世界の食料供給は驚くほど狭い基盤に頼っています。過去1世紀、機械収穫に向き一斉に実る多収品種が選ばれる一方で、特定の谷や乾燥斜面に適応してきた何千もの在来品種が日常の耕作から姿を消しました。しかし遺伝的な画一性には脆弱性があり、広大な地域が似た品種を育てると、新たに進化した1種類の菌や害虫、長期干ばつだけで収穫全体が打撃を受けかねません。野生近縁種や忘れかけた地方品種は、一等農地での収量は控えめでも耐塩性やさび病への抵抗性など育種に不可欠な遺伝子を秘めていることがよくあります。その消失を防ぐため世界の1,700以上のジーンバンクが種子を低温乾燥保存し、北極圏スヴァールバルの永久凍土の岩盤奥深くには停電や洪水、紛争に備えた地球規模の重複保管庫も築かれました。もっとも冷凍保管庫だけでは解決の半分にすぎません。数十年経てば発芽力が落ちるため定期的な植え継ぎが必要であり、1980年に凍らせた種子は変化する気候や害虫と共に進化することも止まるからです。そのため近年は低温保管庫と小規模農家が現地で在来種を育て続ける「生きた」農場ネットワークの両輪で未来の収穫が守られています。

passage.title: How Seed Vaults Guard Crop Diversity Against New Risks
passage.text:
Modern supermarkets create an illusion of boundless agricultural variety, displaying dozens of breads, pastas, and snacks down long aisles. Yet frozen vaults alone are only half the solution. Seeds stored in jars eventually lose germination vigor after decades and must be planted out periodically to produce fresh stock. Moreover, a seed frozen in 1980 stops evolving alongside shifting climates and pests in real fields. Consequently, conservationists increasingly pair cold vaults with "living" on-farm networks, paying smallholder farmers to keep growing traditional varieties in their home landscapes.

Safeguarding tomorrow's harvests requires both the quiet insurance of subzero rock chambers and the ongoing adaptation of working fields.

passage.title: Why Mountain Roads Curve Instead of Climbing Straight
passage.text:
Travelers winding slowly up a mountain pass through a dozen sharp switchbacks sometimes wish engineers had simply cut a straighter road up the slope. On a map, zigzags double the driving distance between the valley floor and the ridge. In steep terrain, however, curving back and forth is what keeps heavy vehicles moving safely in every season.

Physics sets strict limits on road steepness. Once a slope exceeds roughly eight to ten percent, loaded delivery trucks overheat climbing up and risk brake fade coming down, while winter ice turns steep straightaways into dangerous slides. Lengthening the horizontal path through switchbacks spreads the same vertical climb gently across more pavement. (18), ordinary buses and snowplows can serve highland villages year-round.

Curves also help roads survive heavy mountain rain. Water rushing down a long, straight incline gathers speed and gouges out asphalt edges. Switchbacks allow engineers to slant each short segment slightly into side ditches that release water harmlessly onto rocky ledges. (19), retaining walls stay lower and disturb less forest soil.

A winding pass may test a passenger's patience, yet its geometry proves that (20).

Curves also help roads survive heavy mountain rain. Water rushing down a long, straight incline gathers speed and gouges out asphalt edges. Switchbacks allow engineers to slant each short segment slightly into side ditches that release water harmlessly onto rocky ledges. (19), retaining walls stay lower and disturb less forest soil.

A winding pass may test a passenger's patience, yet its geometry proves that (20).

passage.title: How Salt Marshes Buffer Coastal Towns
passage.text:
For centuries, coastal planners viewed tidal salt marshes—flat expanses of mud and tough cordgrass flooded twice a day by the sea—as unproductive wasteland best drained for warehouses or ports. Only after severe storm surges battered concrete seawalls did engineers begin measuring how much quiet protection intact marshes had been providing for free.

When storm waves roll across shallow marsh grass, millions of flexible stems create friction that drains energy from the moving water. Wave-tank experiments and field sensors show that a healthy strip of salt marsh just a hundred meters wide can cut wave height by more than half before water reaches an inland dike. Unlike a rigid concrete wall, which cracks over decades and cannot grow taller as sea levels creep upward, marsh plants trap floating sediment around their roots after high tides. (21), a living marsh can gradually build its own elevation year by year if given room.

Restoring drained marshes requires careful choreography rather than simply knocking down old embankments overnight. If seawater floods subsided land too deeply all at once, cordgrass drowns instead of taking root. Coastal teams therefore open tidal gates gradually or spread clean river silt acquired from harbor dredging to raise the mudflat first. (22), oyster reefs placed along the seaward edge shield young grass seedlings until their roots knit the mud together.

Living shorelines rarely eliminate the need for inner levees in densely populated ports. Even so, pairing engineered dikes with restored marshes gives coastal cities (23).
passage.translation: 何世紀もの間、1日に2度潮に浸かる干潟の塩性湿地は、排水して倉庫や港に造り変えるべき不毛な土地とみなされてきました。激しい高潮がコンクリートの防潮堤を打ち据えて初めて、技術者たちは手つかずの湿地が無償でどれほど大きな防御力を発揮していたかを計測し始めました。高潮の波が浅い湿地の草地を渡るとき、無数のしなやかな茎が摩擦を生んで水のエネルギーを奪います。実験や現地センサーによれば、わずか幅100メートルの健全な塩性湿地があるだけで、内陸の堤防に達する前に波の高さを半分以下に抑えられます。数十年でひび割れ海面上昇に合わせて背を伸ばせない硬いコンクリート壁と異なり、湿地の植物は満潮のたびに根元へ浮遊土砂を捉えます。(21)、十分な余地があれば生きた湿地は年々少しずつ自らの地盤を高くできます。もっとも干拓地の再生は古い堤を一晩で壊せば済むわけではなく、沈下した土地にいきなり深い海水を入れると草が根づく前に溺れてしまいます。そのため水門を段階的に開けたり港の浚渫で出た清浄な砂泥で高さを補ったりします。(22)、沖側の縁にカキ礁を置けば根が泥を固めるまで若い苗を守れます。人口密集港では内側の堤防も依然必要ですが、堤防と再生湿地の組み合わせは沿岸都市に(23)を与えます。

passage.title: Notice About Instrument Acclimatization for the Winter Concert
passage.text:
From: H. Kurosawa, Orchestra Stage Manager
To: String and Woodwind Players
Subject: Instrument delivery and humidity rules at Highland Hall

Dear musicians,
For Sunday's winter symphony concert at Highland Hall, temperatures outside are forecast to stay below freezing all morning, while the stage is heated to twenty-one degrees. Moving wooden string and woodwind instruments straight from icy car trunks onto a warm, sunlit stage can crack spruce soundboards or split clarinets within minutes.

To prevent thermal shock, please arrive through the loading dock by 10:30 a.m. and leave your instruments inside their closed cases in Acclimatization Room B for forty-five minutes before tuning. Staff have set humidifiers in Room B to forty-eight percent so cases warm up gradually.

Cellos and double basses traveling in our equipment van must be loaded at the music school by 8:45 a.m. in hard padded cases; soft fabric gig bags will not be accepted on the van. During the intermission, keep oboes and clarinets swabbed dry and resting on stage stands rather than carrying them out into the cold lobby.

Best regards,
H. Kurosawa
passage.translation: オーケストラ舞台監督の黒沢から弦楽器・木管楽器奏者への連絡。日曜のハイランドホールでの冬季定期演奏会は、午前中ずっと外気温が氷点下の予報である一方、舞台上は21度に暖房されている。凍える車のトランクから暖かい舞台へ木製の弦楽器や木管楽器をいきなり出して載せると、数分で表板の割れやクラリネットのひび割れを招きかねない。急激な温度変化（ヒートショック）を防ぐため、午前10時30分までに搬入口から入り、調弦前の45分間は湿度48％に整えたB順応室でケースを閉じたまま楽器を慣らすこと。機材バンで運ぶチェロとコントラバスは午前8時45分までに音楽学校で緩衝材入りハードケースに入れて積み込むこと（布製のソフトバッグはバンに積載不可）。休憩中はオーボエやクラリネットの管内の水分を拭き取り、冷たいロビーへ持ち出さず舞台上のスタンドに置いておくこと。

第3段落前半の条件と一致。

passage.title: Why Translating Humor Across Languages Is an Art
passage.text:
Automated translation software has grown remarkably adept at turning weather bulletins, user manuals, and shipping contracts from one language into another within seconds. In domains where every term maps cleanly onto a fixed counterpart, literal accuracy is the highest virtue. Hand the same software a comic novel, an animated film script, or a witty newspaper column, however, and the output frequently lands with a dull thud.

Humor rarely resides in dictionary definitions alone. Puns exploit accidental collisions of sound inside a single language: an English joke built on "knight" and "night" evaporates the moment those words become two unrelated nouns in Japanese or Spanish. Comedic timing also leans heavily on grammar. Languages that place the main verb at the very end of a sentence reveal a surprise twist in a different rhythm than languages that announce action upfront. Even cultural assumptions matter—a joke about polite elevator small talk falls flat in places where riders stand in respectful silence.

Skilled literary and audiovisual translators therefore approach comedy closer to musical arrangement than word-for-word substitution. Instead of explaining a pun in an awkward footnote—which kills laughter instantly—a seasoned translator asks what emotional effect the author intended in that scene, then crafts a fresh play on words rooted in the target language's own idioms. Subtitle translators face stricter constraints still: viewers must read the line in three seconds while watching the actor's eyebrows and hearing the cadence of the original voice.

Paradoxically, departing from the literal surface is often the only way to remain faithful to a comic work's spirit. If an original line made readers chuckle at a character's pompous wordplay, a translation that is lexically exact yet lifeless betrays the text far more than an inventive local pun.

Machines may suggest vocabulary candidates quickly, yet sensing why a room laughs still demands human judgment steeped in two living cultures.

passage.title: Why Escalators and Stairs Use Contrasting Step Edges
passage.text:
Commuters hurrying through brightly lit rail stations rarely notice the narrow yellow or metallic strip running along the front edge of every stair and escalator step. Often mistaken for simple trim or anti-slip tape alone, these high-contrast strips—known in accessibility codes as step nosings—play a vital perceptual role in preventing falls.

When an entire staircase is built from uniform gray granite or stainless steel, overhead lighting can make adjacent steps blend visually into a single flat ramp, especially for older adults, tired evening travelers, or people with low vision. Descending stairs requires the brain to judge the exact drop and forward edge of the top and bottom steps within a fraction of a second. Marking each edge with a band whose brightness differs sharply from the tread surface breaks that optical illusion. (18), walkers place their heels more accurately without slowing down.

Color choice matters more than decoration. Pale beige strips on light limestone look stylish in architectural photos, yet offer almost no luminance contrast under cloudy skylight. Building guidelines therefore measure light reflectance values rather than hue alone, ensuring the strip remains distinct even in dim emergency lighting. (19), embedding gritty mineral particles into the nosing strip adds traction right where shoe soles pivot.

Combining visual clarity with physical grip demonstrates how inclusive design (20).
passage.translation: 明るく照らされた鉄道駅を急ぐ通勤客が、階段やエスカレーターの一段ごとの前端に沿って走る細い黄色や金属の帯を意識することはめったにありません。単なる飾りや滑り止めテープと思われがちですが、バリアフリー基準で「段鼻（ノージング）」と呼ばれるこの高コントラストの帯は、転倒を防ぐ重要な知覚的役割を果たしています。階段全体が均一な灰色の御影石やステンレスで造られていると、頭上の照明によって隣り合う段が視覚的に溶け合い、特に高齢者や疲れた夜の乗客、弱視の人には1枚の平らなスロープのように見えてしまうことがあります。階段を下りる際、脳は一瞬のうちに段差と前端の位置を正確に判断しなければなりませんが、踏み面と明るさが大きく異なる帯を端に設けることでこの錯視が解消されます。(18)、歩行者は速度を落とさずに正確な位置へかかとを置けるようになります。重要なのは単なる色味ではなく輝度差であり、淡い石材の上のベージュの帯は写真映えしても曇り空や非常灯の下では見分けがつかないため、建築指針では光の反射率の差を基準にしています。(19)、その帯に鉱物粒子を埋め込むことで靴底が軸足を置くまさにその場所に滑り止め効果も加わります。視覚的明快さと物理的グリップの融合は、インクルーシブデザインがいかに(20)かを示しています。

passage.title: How District Cooling Chills Buildings from Underground Pipes
passage.text:
Walk past a row of glass office towers on a sweltering August afternoon, and you might expect every rooftop to roar with its own bank of air-conditioning condensers. In dense districts of cities such as Sapporo, Stockholm, Toronto, and Singapore, however, many large buildings contain no individual chillers at all. Instead, they draw icy water from a shared underground loop operated by a central "district cooling" plant.

Pooling cooling demand across dozens of offices, hospitals, and shopping arcades unlocks efficiencies that single buildings cannot match. Offices peak at two in the afternoon while hotels need more cooling at night, allowing one central plant to run steady, high-efficiency turbines rather than starting and stopping dozens of small motors. Central plants can also tap natural cold sources unavailable to individual rooftops—such as deep lake water, seawater, or winter snow stored in insulated pits until July. (21), electricity demand during summer heat waves drops sharply.

Urban neighborhoods feel the difference outdoors too. Individual rooftop units pump hot exhaust air straight into narrow streets, worsening the urban heat-island effect right where pedestrians walk. Moving heat rejection to a single waterfront facility keeps downtown air noticeably cooler and quieter. (22), freeing up rooftop space allows architects to install solar panels or shaded sky gardens.

Digging insulated pipe networks beneath existing streets requires heavy upfront investment, so district cooling works best in compact areas. Even so, shared thermal networks offer cities (23).
passage.translation: うだるような8月の午後、ガラス張りのオフィスビル街を歩けばどの屋上でも大型エアコンの室外機がうなりを上げていると思いがちです。しかし札幌、ストックホルム、トロント、シンガポールなどの高密度地区では、個別の冷却機を一切持たず、中央の「地域冷房」プラントから地下配管ループで冷水を受け取っている大型ビルが少なくありません。何十棟ものオフィス、病院、商業施設の冷房需要を束ねることで単独ビルでは不可能な効率が生まれます。オフィスは午後2時にピークを迎える一方ホテルは夜間に需要が増えるため、小型モーターを何十台も発停させる代わりに高効率の大型タービンを安定稼働させられ、深層の湖水や海水、7月まで断熱槽に蓄えた冬の雪といった自然冷熱も活用できます。(21)、夏の猛暑時の電力需要が大幅に下がります。屋外の街並みにも恩恵があり、屋上室外機が狭い通りに熱風を吐き出してヒートアイランド現象を悪化させるのを防ぎ、街なかをより涼しく静かに保てます。(22)、空いた屋上スペースに太陽光パネルや緑豊かな屋上庭園を設けることもできます。既存道路の下に断熱配管を埋設する初期投資は大きいため高密度地区向きですが、共有熱ネットワークは都市に(23)をもたらします。

items.prompt: Why must students attach the furry wind muff when recording outdoors?

Standard foam covers only block indoor breath sounds and fail against outdoor wind noise.

items.translation: 屋外で録音する際に毛足の長い防風マフを装着しなければならないのはなぜですか。

passage.title: Updated Policy for Borrowing Field Recording Kits
passage.text:
From: Media Lab Desk, Faculty of Cultural Studies
To: Undergraduate Fieldwork Students
Subject: Windscreens and memory-card rules for oral-history kits

Dear students,
Starting next Monday, six upgraded stereo audio kits will be available for two-week loan to students conducting local oral-history interviews this semester. Before reserving a kit online, please note two updated borrowing rules based on issues from last autumn.

First, every kit now includes a furry "deadcat" wind muff alongside the standard foam sponge cover. Foam covers stop indoor breath pops, but they cannot block wind rumble on porches, farms, or fishing piers; three outdoor interviews last term were almost impossible to transcribe because of wind noise. Whenever you record outdoors, slip the furry wind muff over the microphone before pressing record.

Second, the Media Lab no longer lends SD memory cards inside the cases. Last year, two students accidentally returned kits before copying their files, and our automatic formatting bench erased a week's worth of recordings. Please purchase your own Class-10 SD card (32 GB or 64 GB) at the campus co-op and test it in the recorder at the pickup counter before leaving.

Happy interviewing,
Media Lab Staff
passage.translation: 文化学部メディアラボ窓口からフィールドワーク履修学生への連絡。来週月曜より、今学期の地域オーラルヒストリー調査向けに新型ステレオ録音キット6台を2週間貸し出す。昨秋のトラブルを踏まえた2つの改定ルールを確認すること。第1に、通常のスポンジ風防に加えて毛足の長い防風マフを同梱した。スポンジは室内の息の音は防げるが縁側や畑、漁港での風切り音は防げず、前学期は屋外録音3件が文字起こし困難になったため、屋外録音時は必ず毛の防風マフを装着すること。第2に、ケース内でのSDカード貸出を廃止した。昨年、データをコピーし忘れたまま返却されたカードが自動初期化機で消去される事故が2件起きたため、生協で各自のSDカードを購入し、貸出窓口で本体に入れて動作確認してから持ち出すこと。

items.prompt: Why did the Media Lab stop lending SD memory cards with the audio kits?

Students returned kits before backing up files, leading to accidental erasure during formatting.
New stereo recorders operate only with cassette tapes.
The campus co-op asked for higher memory-card sales.

distractorReasons: 予算不足が理由ではない。

items.translation: メディアラボが録音キットと一緒にSDメモリーカードを貸し出すのをやめたのはなぜですか。

items.prompt: What was the major advantage of adhesive "perfect binding" when it spread in the twentieth century?
choices: It sped up mass production and made paperback books inexpensive for wide readerships.
It allowed books to survive underwater for centuries.
It enabled piano scores to lie completely flat without any hands.
It eliminated the need for paper in publishing.
items.explanation: 20世紀に大量出版の速度を上げ、何百万人もの読者にとって手頃な価格の本を実現した。
distractorReasons: 第1段落の説明と一致。
水中耐久ではない。
譜面台で平らに開くのは糸かがり綴じの利点。
紙不要ではない。
